title: metsuke v1 — SPO telemetry build
description:
Build epic for the metsuke v1 telemetry pipeline: SPO agent (scrape, spool, sign, upload) and ingest server (verify, archive to S3), per /tmp/metsuke-spec.md collapsed from wayfinder map musashi-ping-sak (decision phase; all 15 map tickets closed). Decision detail lives in musashi-ping-sak.1–15 and docs/research/; accepted decisions in docs/adr/0001–0007. Scaffolding is done and green — tickets start from a working workspace.

## Success Criteria

- An SPO can follow the instructions page from zero to verified uploads: static binary, hardened unit, cold-key or Calidus signing.
- The server verifies, replay-protects, and archives every accepted submission raw in S3; the index is rebuildable from a bucket listing.
- nix flake check stays hermetic and green; the VM test proves the full path on hydraJobs.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .19 .21 .24 .25 .26 .28 .29 .31 .32 .33 .34 .35. No untracked files.

## Intent (.19, .24, .28, .32, .34)

- `src/cli.rs:63` — `--allow-empty` is parsed in the flat flag loop, so `metsuke-server --allow-empty` (serve) and `verify-archive --allow-empty` both succeed and silently drop it; only `main.rs:115` reads it. `cli.rs:33` already scopes it to rebuild-index. Fix: carry it in the variant, `Command::RebuildIndex { allow_empty }`, reject it otherwise; that deletes `Args::allow_empty` and the `match args.allow_empty` re-derivation, and lets `rebuild.rs:10` stop importing `cli::ALLOW_EMPTY` for its error text.
- `src/archive.rs:189,191,200` — the .19 rename left `Archive::store`, `Archive`, `list_keys`; none exist. Fix: `Store::store`, `Store`, `for_each_key`.
- `tests/s3.rs` — .32 deleted `an_endpoint_that_is_not_a_url_is_refused_at_construction`, so the surviving `S3Error::Endpoint` path (`s3.rs:47,60`, `Bucket::new`) has no test. Fix: one case, e.g. `mailto:x`.
- `tests/counters.rs:59,94,107` — `support::counter_store` (`support/mod.rs:118`) not applied where the expression matches exactly. .24 named counters.rs.
- `src/s3.rs:104-107` — comment claims "an answer ... that is not UTF-8" errors. ureq 3.4.0 `Body::read_to_string` sets `lossy_utf8(true)`, so it never does; the bytes are decoded with replacement chars instead. The `BodyExceedsLimit` half is correct. Fix: drop the UTF-8 clause.

Ambiguity, not a finding: .29 named `rebuild()`; `verify.rs:139` still materialises via `keys()` for the audit, with a comment justifying it. Whether audit was in scope is unclear.

## Prose

- `contrib/server.example.toml` — comment blocks are near-verbatim copies of the `config.rs` doc comment on the same field. Verbatim pairs: `:9`/`config.rs:21`, `:13-15`/`:35-37`, `:20`/`:43`, `:26`/`:53`, `:40-41`/`:79-81`, `:49-50`/`:92-93`. `config.rs` owns them. Counterweight: `contrib/config.example.toml` sets the commented-example convention, so trim to what the example alone owns (header, `pool1CHANGEME` note, commented filesystem block) rather than stripping every comment.
- `contrib/server.example.toml:29-30` — "At 1000 keys per page this covers a bucket of a million objects." The code never sets max-keys, so 1000 is the endpoint's default and the arithmetic does not hold on Garage or MinIO. Drop the sentence.
- `tests/rebuild.rs:80-81` — third copy of the unseeded-counters why; owners are `rebuild.rs:12-16` (maintainer) and the `RebuildError::Empty` message at `:50` (operator).
- `tests/s3.rs:520-521` and `:539-540` — second and third copies of the hang-is-worse-than-a-bound why, owned by `s3.rs:212-215`. State the case, not the why.
- `tests/support/mod.rs:141-142` — "The trait split is what keeps this one double" repeats `archive.rs:155-156`.

## Standards and reuse

- `tests/config.rs:73-77` and `:100-104` — the strip-a-field shape hand-rolled twice, alongside `with(field, value)` at `:126`. Extract `without(field)`.

## Gates run this session

- `cargo test --workspace`: 171 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: no warnings, no errors.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `nix flake check` not run.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is `MM`: the two filings below are unstaged. `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code.
- All 12 tickets still `in_progress`, no resolution comments or close reasons — pre-commit, the user's call.
- Decision comments on .25 .26 .29 .35 exist and the diff holds each.
- This map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate.
- Already tracked, not refiled: `hex()` in three places is .23; two more hand-authored listing fixtures noted on .22.

Filed metsuke-4zo.36, metsuke-4zo.37; commented on metsuke-4zo.22.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — five in-scope fixes, of which `cli.rs:63` is the only behaviour change.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All five round-1 in-scope fixes landed and are correct in substance. `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 173 passed / 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean (all four run in this session).

Ten new findings, none blocking on correctness — the first two are the round-1 `cli.rs` fix arriving under-tested.

## Correctness and intent

- `tests/binary.rs:572` — `stderr.contains(ALLOW_EMPTY)` also passes for `ArgsError::Unknown`, because `cli.rs:37`'s usage string embeds `{ALLOW_EMPTY}`. The test cannot distinguish "rejected as misplaced" from "rejected as unknown", so it would not catch the flag regressing to unparsed. Fix: assert on `"only means anything to"`.
- `cli.rs:53-54` says "The flag may be written either side of the subcommand word", but only `rebuild-index --allow-empty` is exercised (`tests/binary.rs:594`). The reversed order is a claim no artifact holds. Fix: add `[ALLOW_EMPTY, REBUILD_INDEX]` to `rebuild_index_on_an_archive_with_nothing_in_it_exits_nonzero`, or a unit test on `Args::parse`.
- `rebuild.rs:48-53` — `RebuildError::Empty` names neither the archive root nor the bucket, yet `EmptyArchive`'s own doc says the case it guards is "a mistyped or unmounted `archive.root`". The operator is asked to decide wrong-path vs really-empty and given nothing to decide on. CLAUDE.md: a message naming what failed and what it got. Fix: `Empty { archive: String }`, filled from the root path or `bucket`.
- `config.rs:54` — `put_retries` is the only numeric field left plain `u32`, and the reason zero is legitimate there lives solely in `tests/config.rs:184`. The module header at `config.rs:1-4` says every field where zero means nothing is a `NonZero`, so a reader at the field cannot tell exception from oversight. Fix: state it in the field's doc comment.

## Prose

- `tests/binary.rs:555-556` — near-verbatim copy of `cli.rs:24-27` ("accepting it there would read as though it did something"), introduced by the round-1 fix. `cli.rs` owns it; the test doc should state the case only.
- `contrib/server.example.toml:3-5` — "What each value means is the doc comment on its field in `crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs`" is false for `bucket` and `region` (`config.rs:41-42`) and `rate_limit_window_secs` (`:91`), which carry no doc comment. Fix the three docs, or soften the pointer.
- `contrib/server.example.toml` — four clauses still duplicate their owner: `:1-2` "nothing here has a default" (`config.rs:1-2`), `:10-12` trailing "which is what keeps this file Nix-managed and public" (`config.rs:35-37`, word for word), `:31-32` "as the allowlist admin command generates them" (`config.rs:79-81`), `:24-25` "so `verify-archive` cannot run against it" (`main.rs:85-87` and `Fatal::CannotVerifyFilesystem`). The env var names at `:10-11` are the example's own and should stay.

## Standards and reuse

- `cli.rs:73,86-90` — `Command::RebuildIndex { allow_empty: false }` is built with a placeholder inside the loop and patched by a second match after it, so the flag is held in two representations and `false` reads the same as a decision. No behaviour bug at any argument ordering (checked bare, both orders, `verify-archive --allow-empty`, two subcommands, repeated subcommand). The fix is strictly smaller code: keep only `named` in the loop, build `Command` once afterwards from `(named.as_deref(), allow_empty)`, and return `AllowEmptyWithoutRebuild` from the non-rebuild arms. Deletes the `taken`/`command` pair and the fix-up match.
- `tests/config.rs:70-88` — `without` and `with` each re-derive `format!("{field} =")` and the same lines/filter/join walk. Fix: one `edited(field, Option<&str>)` where `None` drops the line, or share an `assigns(line, field)` predicate.
- `tests/s3.rs:206-212` — `stored(counter, wire_bytes, signature)` forwards to `stored_submission(key, counter, timestamp, signature, wire_bytes)` with the last two arguments swapped. It compiles only because the types differ. Fix: match the helper's order, or delete the forwarder and call `stored_submission` at the four sites.

## Beads hygiene

- I staged `.beads/` with `git add -A` so `nix flake check` would evaluate the whole tree; the review changed no code. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is `MM` again from this round's comment — `git add .beads/` before committing.
- All 12 tickets still `in_progress`, no resolution comments or close reasons: pre-commit, the user's call.
- Round-2 filings: none. Every finding above is this diff's own work. The cross-crate `value()` duplication in the two `cli.rs` files went to .23 as a comment, where the ureq-builder and `hex()` duplication already lives.

Verdict: correctness is sound and every gate is green. Blocking nothing; the two `cli.rs` test gaps are the items worth fixing before /commit, since they are the round-1 fix's own coverage.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 3. All ten round-2 fixes landed and are correct. Gates re-run in this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` 173 passed / 0 failed; clippy `--deny warnings` silent; fmt clean. Verified directly, not taken on report: `Args::parse` produces the right `Command` or error at every ordering (bare `--allow-empty`, both orders with `rebuild-index`, both with `verify-archive`, two subcommands, a repeated subcommand, `--config

--allow-empty`, no args), and no arm in the final `match (named.as_deref(), allow_empty)` shadows another. `S3Archive::location()` leaks nothing: `Bucket::base_url()` is the endpoint plus bucket path, with signing done per-action, so no credential or presigned query reaches the error text. `stored(..)` has 11 call sites, not nine; all pass the new order. Two findings worth acting on, one filed, one design call. ## In-scope - `tests/binary.rs:389-395` — the `[archive] kind = "s3"` block is hand-written here, while `contrib/server.example.toml` now owns it and `tests/config.rs::example()` reads it. This round added `signature_validity_secs`, `put_retry_backoff_ms` and `list_max_pages` to five places: that block, `tests/config.rs:113-116`, `tests/config.rs:153-155`, `tests/s3.rs:188-191`, and the example. Shotgun Surgery, and it is .24's own shape ("Server test fixtures re-authored per test file"). Fix: build the binary test's block from `example()` with an `endpoint`/`put_retries` substitution, and let one field list drive the two in `tests/config.rs`. - `src/config.rs:53-55`, `tests/config.rs:188-189`, `src/s3.rs:37-38` — the why for `put_retries` being the non-`NonZero` exception is now in three places. Round 2 asked for the fact to move to the field; it was added there without the test's copy being cut. `config.rs` owns it. Fix: `tests/config.rs:188` -> "Zero loads; every other number in this file is a `NonZero`", and drop the `s3.rs` field doc's ADR clause. Optional prose trims, same axis, lower value: `src/archive.rs:165-167` retells the mistyped-vs-empty ambiguity that `rebuild::EmptyArchive` owns (a pointer would do); `tests/config.rs:10-11` repeats `:17-19`; `tests/config.rs:84-86` and `src/cli.rs:52-53` narrate the lines below them. The one claim in `cli.rs:52` worth keeping is "either side of the subcommand word" — that is grammar the code does not state and `tests/binary.rs` now checks. ## Design call, your decision `List::location()` drew a split verdict. Against: a description of where the archive lives is not part of the listing capability, so it is a third concern on the .19 seam; its only caller is one error arm; the test double must invent `"the test archive"`; and two unrelated shapes (a path, `"{name} at {url}"`) are flattened to `String`. For: both callers already hold `impl List`, so a separate trait adds a bound and buys nothing, and threading the location from `main.rs::dispatch` instead would need another parameter because `run` has already destructured the config. My recommendation is keep it as is — the objection is real but the alternative is more machinery for the same string. ## Filed metsuke-4zo.38 — `ratelimit.rs` and `intake.rs` cast `NonZeroU64` seconds to `i64` unchecked; above `i64::MAX` the rate limiter never fires and the skew check rejects everything. Unreachable except by an absurd literal, filed rather than fixed here because `.21`'s ask was zero and this is the ceiling. Not re-reported: `verify::audit` still materialising via `keys()` (round-1 ambiguity, and .36/.37 hold the audit's cost); `dispatch`'s `verify_archive` closure (.33 asked for that shape). ## Beads hygiene `.beads/` is staged with the code. All 12 tickets still `in_progress` with no resolution comments or close reasons — pre-commit, your call. Nothing committed. Verdict: ready for /commit. The two in-scope items above are cleanups, not blockers; neither changes behaviour, and every gate is green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .88 .89 .90 .91 .92 .93 and the .100 rework (.96 .97 folded in). No untracked files; every new file is `git add`ed, several with unstaged edits on top, so `nix flake check` saw the whole tree.

Gates run in this session: `nix flake check` -> all checks passed; `cargo test --workspace` all green (0 failed); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` silent; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.

Verified directly rather than taken on report: the v2 body framing costs one byte per line and `upload_batch_max_bytes` (4194304) now equals the server's `max_decompressed_bytes` (4194304), so .96's wedge is closed by construction; `zstd` on the committed recording measures 450881 -> 35002 bytes, so a 4 MiB raw batch has ~3x headroom against `max_body_bytes = 1048576` and the compressed dimension is not a second wedge. .97 is held by `the_node_root_severity_comes_from_the_agents_own_floor`. The `--unit` filter means the severity floor never reaches another unit's journal, so `namespace_roots` not bounding the floor is not a widening.

## Standards and ADRs

- `CLAUDE.md:19` — `The agent touches only the loopback Prometheus endpoint: no socket, no journal, no groups — docs/adr/0007` is now false: with `[log]` set, `nix/unit.nix:42` gives the unit `SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal`. ADR 0010 also has no invariant line at all, though the header says "Each is an accepted decision; read the ADR before working near it." Fix: reword the 0007 line as its no-`[log]` posture and add a 0010 line. This is .94's own second half.
- `docs/adr/0007-*.md:3` is `Status: accepted` while `docs/adr/0010:3` says `supersedes ADR 0007`, and 0010 is `proposed` while its code ships. Your decision (.94 calls it a human one): mark 0007 superseded-by-0010 and 0010 accepted, or hold the commit.
- `crates/metsuke-server/src/instructions.rs:321-323` — the node-config snippet hand-writes `Consensus.LeiosKernel`, `Consensus.LeiosPeer`, `Forge.Loop.AdoptedBlock` while the agent's selection prefixes live in `contrib/config.example.toml`. `root_severity` is read from that file; the namespaces are not, against the module header's "no edit here can document a default the agent does not ship". They agree today; nothing holds them there, and drift means the operator gets zero lines with nothing saying so. Fix: a test asserting every shipped `namespaces` entry is covered by a snippet key or the root severity, beside `the_node_root_severity_comes_from_the_agents_own_floor`.
- `crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:104` — `open_spool` sets only `busy_timeout`, so both connections to the one file use the default rollback journal and take exclusive locks against each other. `nix/unit-test.nix:346` already works around it ("the agent is writing the same file and a reader meets its lock"). Fix: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` in `open_spool`, which both `Spool` and `LogSpool` go through.
- `crates/metsuke-wire/src/envelope.rs:273-278` — "A trace line must not hold a raw newline ... Free rather than checked" does not hold: `Payload::Lines { lines: Vec<String> }` is public with a public field, so a line holding `\n` is representable and `open` splits it into two under a valid signature. Silent reframing of an archived object is worse than the error the check would raise. Fix: reject the newline in `body()` as a `SealError`, or give `Lines` a validated line type.

## Silent failures and implicit values

- `crates/metsuke/src/logtail.rs:73-77` — a spool write failure only `eprintln!`s and breaks the drain; `run` then sleeps `respawn_backoff` and starts over forever, so a full disk or a corrupt spool never reaches `main`, which treats spool *open* failure as fatal at `main.rs:135`. With no WAL a transient `SQLITE_BUSY` takes the same branch and costs 30 s of stream. Fix: separate the two — retry a busy push, and let a persistent spool failure terminate the process the way startup does.
- `crates/metsuke/src/config.rs:133` — `default_journalctl_path()` is `PathBuf::from("journalctl")`, a PATH lookup, contradicting `logsource.rs:24`'s own "a hardened unit's PATH is not something to rely on". A non-NixOS operator who sets `[log]` without the path gets a spawn error logged every 30 s rather than a startup failure; the NixOS module already supplies an absolute path. Fix: require `journalctl_path` alongside `journal_unit`.
- `scripts/record-v1-envelope.sh:75` — `(cd "$scratch" && cargo run --quiet 2>/dev/null) >"$out"` truncates the fixture before the run and discards every compile/run error, so a failed re-record leaves an empty `v1-envelope.hex` and no reason. This is the frozen-wire guard. Fix: drop `2>/dev/null`, write to a temp file, `mv` on success.
- `scripts/record-trace-fixtures.sh:197` — `startup_end` is empty when `"ns":"Consensus.LeiosKernel.Msg"` is absent, and the failure surfaces as a bare `sed` error; only `BlockForged` and `Announcement` are asserted above. Fix: assert the `Msg` line with the other two.

## Prose

- `contrib/config.example.toml:63-66` re-derives ADR 0010's namespace_roots security argument ("The agent can read every unit's journal, so the roots are what bounds how far a namespace rule reaches into it"), which ADR 0010's Decision owns. `logselect.rs::SelectConfig::new` has the right shape — "ADR 0010 says why". Same for `:39-42`'s framing/decompress-measure reasoning, which ADR 0010's Decision also owns; `delivery.rs:24-28` is at the site and stays. Fix: the example points at the ADR and keeps only the operator instruction ("set it to the server's value or under").

## Reuse

- `crates/metsuke/tests/logtail.rs:30` and `crates/metsuke/tests/logselect.rs:30` — `shipped_rules()` written twice, both parsing the same minimal TOML and building the same `SelectConfig`. `tests/support/mod.rs` was touched by this diff already. Fix: move it there.

## Filed

Commented on metsuke-4zo.101 (per-line commit and uncached statements on the same write path it names), metsuke-4zo.85 (the recorder preamble now has three copies), metsuke-4zo.98 (journalctl exit status discarded in `Drop`, and `logselect::severity` dropping an unknown spelling with nothing counting it). No new tickets: every finding that is not this diff's job had an owner already.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is ` M` — unstaged. `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code.
- .88 .90 .92 are still `in_progress` and .89 .91 .93 .96 .97 .100 still `open`, all six implemented in this tree, with no resolution comments or close reasons. Pre-commit, your call.
- Fixtures are files in the repo referenced by path, not pasted into bodies. `.beads` is in sync after the flush.

Verdict: not ready for `/commit`. `CLAUDE.md:19` states an invariant the tree breaks, and the ADR 0007/0010 status pair needs your decision; the rest are the eight fixes above, of which the WAL pragma, the logtail spool-failure split, and the newline check are behaviour changes.

title: Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core
description:
## What to build

The shared wire contract both crates trust: envelope types (schema_version starting at 1, pool_id, agent_version, replay counter, timestamp, samples with the 8 nullable v1 fields), zstd compression, and raw detached Ed25519 sign/verify over the compressed body bytes (ADR 0001). Exposed as a library from the metsuke crate so the server consumes the identical types and defaults — reviewers verify one definition, not two copies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Property test: envelope encode→decode roundtrip.
- [ ] Property test: sign→verify roundtrip, and any tampered byte in the compressed body rejects.
- [ ] Replay counter and timestamp sit inside the signed payload (ADR 0002).
- [ ] metsuke-server can depend on the metsuke crate as a library.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: seal/open wire core with property tests; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: envelope schema v1 (PoolId opaque type, 8 nullable sample fields) with seal/open as the whole wire interface — seal = JSON+zstd+Ed25519 sign, open = verify_strict before bounded decompress (ADR 0001/0002). Property tests: seal→open roundtrip, tamper rejects, PoolId bech32 roundtrip; unit tests for size cap, NaN, malformed/wrong-prefix/wrong-length pool ids. Server depends on metsuke by path; crate versions decoupled per ADR 0006. Filed metsuke-9a1 (deferred metsuke-wire extraction).

title: Developer data endpoints
description:
## What to build

Developer pull access to the archive without per-dev AWS credentials: a single basic-auth user (user in config, password in a LoadCredential file — decided in metsuke-4zo.75, superseding this ticket's original "sops EnvironmentFile"), a listing route (prefix and after filters, JSON from the SQLite index) and a download route streaming the raw S3 object. Read-only, no transformation — developers get the same self-verifying bytes the bucket holds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing or wrong credentials → 401 on both routes.
- [ ] Listing filters by prefix and after; results come from the index, not a live bucket scan.
- [ ] Download streams the object byte-identical to what was archived.
      Byte-identical holds; streaming does not — it ships buffered, tracked in metsuke-4zo.72.

## Blocked by

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index.
close_reason: developer listing and download routes behind one basic-auth account

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .10 (developer data endpoints). No untracked files; all 28 changes staged.

## Silent failures

- `src/main.rs:327-338` — a zero-byte or newline-only credential file yields the working credential `metsuke-dev:`, opening both routes to anyone who reads the public config. The function doc at :325-327 names exactly this hazard ("the routes would otherwise be open on a credential nobody set") and does not close it. Fix: after the trim, reject an empty password with a `Fatal` variant naming the path.
- `src/developer.rs:173` — `String::from_utf8_lossy(&decoded).into_owned()`. A non-UTF-8 percent escape in `prefix`, `after` or `key` becomes U+FFFD, so the server answers a different query than the client sent, with a 200. The function doc at :149-151 promises the opposite ("stays as written ... fails at the filter"). Fix: `String::from_utf8` and 400 on the error.
- `src/http.rs:203-211` — `challenge` logs only the path. No header, wrong scheme, undecodable base64, no colon, and wrong password are one line to the operator. Withholding the reason from the client is justified at the site (`developer::Unauthorized`); withholding it from the journal is not, and CLAUDE.md asks for a message naming what failed and what it got. Fix: give `Unauthorized` a private reason and pass it as `refuse_withholding`. The mechanism is already there.

## Intent

- `src/http.rs:183` — `(_, SUBMISSIONS_PATH) | (_, OBJECT_PATH) => refuse(None, 405, ...)` answers before authentication, so a non-GET confirms the routes exist unauthenticated. The acceptance criterion is "Missing or wrong credentials -> 401 on both routes". Fix: match the developer paths on path alone, authorize, then answer 405.

## Prose

- `tests/developer.rs:16` — `const PASSWORD: &str = "hunter2"` is a second copy of `support/mod.rs:356 DEVELOPER_PASSWORD`, whose own comment says "One place, so the unit tests and the spawned binary authenticate as the same account". `tests/binary.rs:22` imports it; this file already imports from `support`. Fix: `use support::DEVELOPER_PASSWORD as PASSWORD`, drop the local const.
- `tests/archive.rs:130-132` — second copy of the why owned by the `Bytes` trait doc at `src/archive.rs:201-203` (a developer verifies the signature over these bytes, so any transformation is unverifiable). Fix: state what the test checks, drop the justification.

## Gates run this session

- `nix flake check` -> all checks passed.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 286 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings`: silent.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is `MM` from this round: `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code.
- .10 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason: pre-commit, your call.
- The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate.
- Not re-reported, already tracked: .72 (download buffers the whole object), .73 (download stalls ingest), .74 (no rate limit on the developer routes), .24 (test fixtures re-authored per file, which the `support` rewrite here is doing).

## Filed

metsuke-4zo.75 (needs-decision) — the ticket says credentials arrive by sops EnvironmentFile; the implementation reads `password_file` and its own prose says LoadCredential. Which shape wins?

Verdict: not ready for /commit. `main.rs:327` is the one blocker; the other five are small.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All six round-1 fixes landed and are correct in substance — verified directly, not taken on report: `main.rs::developer` trims `\r\n` then refuses empty; `query_value` returns `Result<_, BadQuery>` and the download uses it too; `challenge` puts the reason in `refuse_withholding`'s withheld channel and only "credentials required" in the body; `route` matches path, authorizes, then checks method.

Five findings, all test coverage and one prose. None changes behaviour.

title: Rework the v2 trace payload to JSONL framing and string selection
description:
## What to build

Rework the uncommitted v2 trace payload before it is committed. v2 has never shipped, so the wire is free to change today and frozen after.

1. **JSONL framing.** Body is a JSON header line, then the selected trace lines appended raw, then zstd, then the existing detached Ed25519 over the compressed bytes. Deletes the JSON-in-JSON-string escaping (measured 1.1095x) and the `Payload` untagged enum with its "a third variant must introduce a new key" trap. v1 stays byte-identical: `serde_json::to_string` emits no newlines, so a v1 body is exactly one line and "parse the first line as the header" reads both versions.
2. **String selection, no JSON decode on the line path.** `ns` is the first `"ns":"`; it precedes `data`, so nothing nested shadows it. `sev` is the *last* `"sev":"`; `data` precedes it and the keys after it are flat. Deletes `logselect`'s `Unreadable` outcome. Rests on the node key order in `crates/metsuke/tests/fixtures/recordings/leios-node-traces.log` -- the recording is the guard, so a node bump that reorders fails the fixture test.
3. **`namespace_roots` bound in `[log]`.** A local ceiling on what this host will ever ship. Nothing pushes rules yet (metsuke-4zo.99), but under ADR 0010 the agent reads every unit's journal, so the ceiling is the field that makes .99 additive instead of a wire break.
4. **metsuke-4zo.96 and .97.** Budget the batch against the bytes actually sent rather than a second measure, and pin the node root severity on the instructions page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A trace line is shipped byte-for-byte as the node emitted it.
- [ ] No `serde_json` call touches a trace line in the agent.
- [ ] v1 wire bytes unchanged, proved by the existing `v1-envelope.hex` cassette.
- [ ] The agent-side batch budget and the server's decompress limit cannot disagree.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace`, `clippy --deny warnings`, `fmt --check`, `nix flake check` all green.

## Out of scope

- metsuke-4zo.95 (pipe line source) -- second implementation behind the same seam, later.
- metsuke-4zo.99 (server pushes namespaces on ACK) -- needs its own ADR.
- metsuke-4zo.98 (loss invisible in the archive) -- report if touched, do not build.
- Flipping ADR 0007's status or CLAUDE.md's invariant list -- the owner's call.
close_reason: v2 is JSONL framing with string selection, no JSON on the line path

comments.text: Shipped: JSONL v2 framing, string selection with no serde_json on the line path, namespace_roots as the host ceiling, and .96/.97 folded in. Gates green including both NixOS VM tests and the devnet e2e against a real Leios node.

title: LogSpool::push evicts via a full-table window scan on every insert
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:push_capped (used by LogSpool::push). The FIFO-eviction DELETE recomputes SUM(bytes) OVER (ORDER BY id DESC) across the whole table on every single push, inside the write transaction. Sample pushes are one per sample_interval_secs (cheap); trace-line pushes are one per selected journal line, so under sustained trace volume this is an O(n) scan per insert, O(n^2) to fill the spool to log_max_bytes (default 256MiB, potentially ~1M small rows). Not measured at runtime — flagging from reading the query plan, not a timed regression.
Fix: keep a running byte total (e.g. a one-row counter table updated in the same transaction) so eviction reads only the oldest rows actually being dropped, not the whole table.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Same function, write-path cost beyond the eviction scan (from review of the uncommitted trace tree):

- push_capped opens its own transaction per call, so LogSpool::push commits once per selected line: one fsync per line of an unbounded stream. A push_many taking a slice, plus a small buffer in logtail::drain, makes it one commit per flush.
- The INSERT and DELETE SQL are format!'d and Connection::execute re-prepares them on every call. Stream's fields are already &'static str: carry insert/evict as consts on Stream and use prepare_cached.

Not measured at runtime; both are structural, same as the scan this ticket names.

title: outstanding_rows scans and writes the whole table on every upload tick
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:outstanding_rows, both streams, every tick.

- Unconditional `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE bytes > ?1` before the read. No index on `bytes`, so it is a full scan plus a write lock contending with the trace thread's connection, run even when the table is empty. The size is already known at push_capped, where the row could be refused instead.
- The read filters `SUM(bytes) OVER (ORDER BY id)` outside the window, so SQLite scans every row to return a bounded oldest prefix.

Distinct from metsuke-4zo.101, which is push_capped's eviction. Fix: guard the delete with `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1` or move it to push; read `ORDER BY id LIMIT ?` and accumulate the budget in Rust.

title: Agent test constants and spool builders are re-authored per test file
description:
crates/metsuke/tests/support/mod.rs exists and this diff adds #![allow(dead_code)] to it, but the new tests copy instead:

- `UNBOUNDED = 64 * 1024 * 1024` in tests/agent.rs, delivery.rs, logtail.rs, uploader.rs (and `WHOLE_SPOOL` in spool.rs); `NO_CONTENTION` four times.
- Four LogSpool builders: `test_log_spool` (agent.rs), `temp_log_spool` (delivery.rs), `temp_log_config` (spool.rs), inline in logtail.rs.
- `samples_of`/`lines_of` (delivery.rs) re-inlined as `let Payload::.. else { panic! }` in agent.rs, uploader.rs, logtail.rs.

Same shape metsuke-4zo.24 fixed for the server tests. Fix: move all of it into support.

title: The commented config example is hand-parsed at three seams
description:
Reading a value back out of contrib/config.example.toml is written three ways:

- metsuke-server/src/instructions.rs `agent_min_severity` strips "# " and `strip_prefix` for one key.
- metsuke-server/tests/instructions.rs `shipped_namespaces` does it with a different needle, then parses TOML.
- metsuke/tests/config.rs `uncomment` already generalises the uncomment step.

toml is a dependency of both crates. Fix: one `uncomment(example) -> String` plus a `toml::Table` lookup, used by all three, so no seam trims quotes by hand.

title: ADR 0010 declares it supersedes ADR 0007, but 0007 and CLAUDE.md still say otherwise
description:
docs/adr/0010-log-based-trace-collection.md status line: "supersedes ADR 0007". docs/adr/0007 is untouched and CLAUDE.md's invariant list still reads "The agent touches only the loopback Prometheus endpoint: no socket, no journal, no groups — docs/adr/0007".

On commit the repo asserts both. metsuke-4zo.100 reserved flipping 0007's status and the invariant list as the owner's call, so the supersession claim currently has no counterpart.

Question: mark ADR 0007 superseded and rewrite the CLAUDE.md invariant, or drop "supersedes ADR 0007" from 0010's status line until you do?

title: Envelope::new takes six positional arguments, so a header field is a sweep
description:
`envelope::Envelope::new` (crates/metsuke-wire/src/envelope.rs) takes pool_id,
agent_id, agent_version, counter, timestamp, payload positionally. Adding
`agent_id` in metsuke-jfb.3 meant editing all ten call sites across three
crates; this epic adds header fields by design.

The private `Header` struct in the same file already groups exactly the
non-payload fields. Fix: make it the argument, so the next field is one
struct-literal edit per site rather than a sweep.

Do this before metsuke-4zo.79, which reshapes the same seam.

title: Instructions page
description:
## What to build

The SPO onboarding surface: one static HTML page (no JS, no CSS effort) rendered at server build time from a template whose every code-owned value — intervals, port, flake output names, latest client version, the exact field list that leaves the box — is pulled from the file that owns it at compile, so documentation can never drift from shipped defaults (ADR 0006). Outline per musashi-ping-sak.14: intro and fields, register, choose signing key, enable PrometheusSimple, install, configure, systemd, verify, staying up to date. Numbered copy-paste steps take an SPO from zero to verified uploads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Page builds from the files that own the shipped values, never a retyped copy. The agent's defaults reach it through contrib/config.example.toml and its unit through contrib/metsuke.service, both carried whole; the link to the code is crates/metsuke/tests/config.rs (defaults) and checks.instructions-outputs (flake output names), which fail loud. Amended from "client-crate constants": a direct pull would make metsuke-server depend on metsuke, which the crate-independence invariant forbids.
- [ ] The exact v1 field list appears on the page.
- [ ] All outline sections present, each step copy-pasteable.
- [ ] Served by the ingest server as static content.

## Blocked by

Client binary end-to-end; Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.
close_reason: Instructions page rendered from the shipped config and unit, served at /

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .11 (instructions page). One staged
artifact that is not source, seven substantive fixes, eight prose trims.

## Staged, not source

`result-1` -> `/nix/store/hfydnkrwa87mqp0hkc12hjr62749sz3a-metsuke-server-alone-test-0`,
`git add`ed as a symlink. `.gitignore` has `/result`, not `result-1`. Fix: `git rm --cached
result-1 && rm result-1`, and `/result-*` in `.gitignore`. Nothing else is untracked, so
the gates below evaluated the real tree.

## Correctness

- `tests/binary.rs:718` — the new test was spliced inside an existing doc comment. `///
  Developer pull access is gated on the one credential (ticket` now heads
  `the_instructions_page_is_served_without_credentials`, and `/// metsuke-4zo.10): both
  routes, no credentials, nothing read.` dangles above
  `both_developer_routes_refuse_a_request_without_credentials`. Fix: move the new test
  below that function and rejoin the two lines.
- `src/http.rs:185` — `_ => refuse(None, 405, format!("{} takes GET", instructions::PATH))`
  has no test. The only 405 assertion in `tests/` is `SUBMIT_PATH`'s
  (`tests/binary.rs:715`), and the new test exercises GET only. Fix: assert `POST /` -> 405
  in `the_instructions_page_is_served_without_credentials`.
- `src/instructions.rs:225` — `port_or_known_default()` returns `Some(80)` for any `http://`
  URL, so the `.expect("the example metrics_url has a port")` below it cannot fire for a
  port-less URL; it fires only for an unknown scheme. If the example's `:12798` is ever
  dropped, the page renders `PrometheusSimple 127.0.0.1 80` and a `curl` against port 80 as
  fact. Fix: `.port()`, which is `None` when the URL states no port.
- `flake.nix:307` — both loops in `instructions-outputs` pass vacuously when `grep -o`
  matches nothing: empty list, body never runs, `touch $out`. Both patterns match today (I
  ran them: `metsuke-static-{aarch64,x86_64}-linux`, `nixosModules.metsuke`), so the check
  is real now and silently stops being real on a rename or a reflow of those literals. Fix:
  capture each grep to a variable and `[ -n "$names" ] || exit 1` before the loop.

## Page claims an operator would act on

- `src/instructions.rs:177` — "samples taken while the agent was down upload afterwards".
  Nothing samples while it is down; `crates/metsuke/src/main.rs:105` is the only sample
  site and it is inside the loop. What survives is unacked rows taken before the stop. Fix:
  "samples not yet acked upload afterwards."
- `src/instructions.rs:135` — "Every commented line is the shipped default" is false for `#
  signing_key = "/etc/metsuke/pool.skey"`. `crates/metsuke/tests/config.rs:85` excludes
  exactly that line, with the comment "The signing_key line documents the flag interplay,
  not a default." An operator reads it as the default location. Fix: name the exception.
- `src/instructions.rs:158` — "one line per upload attempt". `crates/metsuke/src/main.rs:122`
  is `Ok(None) => return config.upload_interval`, which logs nothing when the spool is
  empty. Fix: "one line per upload."

## Prose

- Same why in three places: `src/http.rs:3-4` (module header, "the onboarding page an
  operator reads before they have any of it"), `src/http.rs:175-176` (route comment),
  `tests/binary.rs:719-720`. Owner is the route comment — it sits on the code that grants
  the access. Fix: header down to "and the `instructions` page"; delete the test's second
  clause.
- Same why in three places: `src/instructions.rs:1-6` (header), `:36` (`render`'s "so a test
  can see the page follow them"), `tests/instructions.rs:1-3`. Owner is the module header.
  Fix: drop `render`'s rationale, keep the test header's pointer.
- `src/instructions.rs:192-194` (escape's "keeps a `<` in a config from swallowing the rest
  of a step") and `tests/instructions.rs:123-124` ("silently swallow the rest of a step").
  Owner is the test. Fix: one sentence on the function.
- `src/instructions.rs:2` "in nine steps" and `tests/instructions.rs:11` "The nine steps"
  both restate `const SECTIONS: [&str; 9]`, which holds the count. CLAUDE.md: "Digits live
  in exactly one file." Fix: drop "nine" from both.
- `src/instructions.rs:29-31` — `page()`'s "Panics only if a file compiled in above stopped
  carrying what the page reads out of it" retells the five `.expect` strings below. Fix:
  keep only the pointer to `tests/instructions.rs`.
- `src/main.rs:310` — "Rendered before the listener" states the order of the two lines under
  it. Fix: keep from "it is built from files compiled in".
- `tests/binary.rs:698-699` — "and a known route reached with the wrong method is named
  rather than hidden" repeats `http.rs:187-188`, and describes the 405 half while sitting on
  the 404 setup. Fix: keep "Not the root: that is the instructions page."

## Standards

- `tests/instructions.rs:89,106,107` — `"127.0.0.1:12798"`, `"/usr/local/bin/metsuke"` and
  `"/etc/metsuke/config.toml"` are restated from `contrib/config.example.toml:9` and
  `contrib/metsuke.service`. CLAUDE.md: "Digits live in exactly one file." A stale needle
  makes `.replace` a no-op and the next assert fails, so this is Shotgun Surgery rather than
  a silent bug. Fix: read the needle out of `instructions::CONFIG_EXAMPLE`/`UNIT`, or a
  pointer comment at each literal.

## Decision, yours

AC 1 reads "Page builds from client-crate constants; changing a default in code changes the
page with no manual edit." The page pulls the intervals and the metrics port out of
`contrib/config.example.toml`, not the client crate: changing `sample_interval_secs`'s
default in `crates/metsuke/src/config.rs` fails `crates/metsuke/tests/config.rs:69` and then
still needs a manual contrib edit. Pulling directly would make metsuke-server depend on
metsuke, which CLAUDE.md forbids ("neither depends on the other"). Flake output names have
the same shape, guarded by the new `instructions-outputs` check instead. My recommendation:
keep the contrib route and amend the AC to name the two checks as the link — both gates fail
loud, and the alternative breaks a stated invariant.

## Gates, run this session

- `cargo test --workspace`: 304 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings`: silent.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `nix flake check`: all checks passed (with `result-1` staged).

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is modified and unstaged — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the
code. .11 is `in_progress` with no resolution comment and no close reason; pre-commit, your
call. The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to
graduate.

## Filed

None. Every finding above is this diff's own work.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — unstage `result-1`, then the four correctness items and the
three false page claims. The prose and standards items are cleanups.

My round-1 fix asked for a pointer and this is where a pointer leads; the five `.expect` strings already say what each means. Every commented setting below them is the shipped default" is `contrib/config.example.toml:1-3`; "The exception is `signing_key` … pass the key as a credential" is `:14-17`. The config file owns both — it lands on the operator's disk, where the page does not. Fix: "Write this to `{config_path}`; its own comments say which values you must set." - `src/instructions.rs:145` — "Put it in `/etc/systemd/system/metsuke.service`" is `contrib/metsuke.service:5-7`, again rendered directly below. `:144` "with no privileges beyond reading its own config and writing its spool" restates the `DynamicUser`/`Protect*`/`Restrict*` block in the same `

title: Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit
description:
## What to build

Distribution as declared in the spec — Nix-flake-only, no install script ever: static musl flake outputs metsuke-static-x86_64-linux and metsuke-static-aarch64-linux cross-built via crane, a NixOS module for the agent and one for the server (all spec limits exposed as module options, never hardcoded), and an example hardened unit at contrib/metsuke.service (DynamicUser, ProtectSystem=strict, StateDirectory, no groups — ADR 0007) with the LoadCredential variant documented as optional.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both static outputs build; binaries link no dynamic libraries.
- [ ] Agent module renders config TOML from options; server module exposes every limit as an option.
- [ ] contrib unit committed; agent runs under it against a loopback endpoint with no extra privileges.
- [ ] nix flake check remains hermetic and green.

## Blocked by

Client binary end-to-end.
close_reason: Static builds, both NixOS modules, hardened unit and a VM test covering all four

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .12. No untracked files; all nine changes staged.

## Intent

- `nix/server-module.nix:60-77` — only `listen` and `index_path` are declared options; every limit rides `freeformType = toml.type`. AC: "server module exposes every limit as an option" / "all spec limits exposed as module options, never hardcoded". Unexposed: `ingest.max_body_bytes`, `max_decompressed_bytes`, `rate_limit_uploads`, `rate_limit_window_secs`, `max_timestamp_skew_secs`, `calidus.query_timeout_secs`, `resolution_ttl_secs`, `developer.list_max_rows`, and all of `S3Config` (`request_timeout_secs`, `signature_validity_secs`, `put_retries`, `put_retry_backoff_ms`, `list_max_pages`). Counterweight, verified: every struct in `crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs` carries `deny_unknown_fields` (:17,70,93,120,133,143,183), so a misspelled freeform key fails at startup naming itself — what freeform costs is eval-time typing and a discoverable option surface, not safety. Fix: nested submodules mirroring the Rust structs, freeform kept for `applications`. Same shape on `nix/agent-module.nix:39-58`, where the twelve defaulted fields in `crates/metsuke/src/config.rs` are all freeform.
- `nix/unit-test.nix:545-586` — AC 3 reads "contrib unit committed; agent runs under it against a loopback endpoint with no extra privileges". The test runs `services.metsuke`, the module's generated unit; `contrib/metsuke.service`'s own `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/metsuke` is never executed. `checks.contrib-unit` ties the two at the hardening block, but they are not identical (the module adds `LoadCredential`, contrib does not). Either start the contrib file verbatim with the binary symlinked to `/usr/local/bin/metsuke`, or say in the close reason that the AC is met by shared `nix/unit.nix` plus the diff gate.
- `flake.nix:276-282` — `checks.units` is a `pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest`, so `nix flake check` now needs `/dev/kvm`. .14 states the VM gate is "excluded from nix flake check (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network)". This test is no-node and no-network, so it is not the thing .14 excluded, but it is a VM and it makes flake check machine-dependent. Your call: keep it in `checks`, or move it to `hydraJobs` beside .14's.

## Correctness

- `nix/server-module.nix:408` — `credentialPath = name: "/run/credentials/metsuke-server.service/${name}"` types the unit name a second time; `systemd.services.metsuke-server` at :480 is the first. A rename breaks the config paths with no eval error. The comment above says both halves derive from one list, which is true of the names and false of the unit. Fix: `unitName = "metsuke-server"`, used in both, and one clause saying why the literal path rather than `\$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY` (a TOML file gets no expansion).
- `nix/unit-test.nix:651` — \`assert set(field("Groups")) <= set(field("Gid"))\` cannot fail for the directive it guards: \`DynamicUser=true\` alone yields an empty supplementary Groups line, so deleting \`SupplementaryGroups = ""\` from \`nix/unit.nix\` leaves it green. It catches added groups, which is not what ADR 0007 turns on. Fix: grant the service a group in a second node and assert the test notices, or narrow the docstring to what it checks.

## Reuse

- `flake.nix:164-175` — `staticArgs` re-types `version`, `strictDeps`, `doCheck`, `src` and `cargoExtraArgs`, all of which `binaryArgs` (:127-131) and the `metsuke` package five lines below already set identically. Only `cargoArtifacts` genuinely differs. Fix: \`removeAttrs binaryArgs [ "cargoArtifacts" ] // { src = agentSrc; cargoExtraArgs = "--package metsuke"; CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS = ...; }\`.

## Prose

- `nix/unit.nix:3-4` — "no groups, so a compromise reaches a metrics page and nothing else" is a second copy of ADR 0007's Consequences ("compromise of the agent yields read access to a metrics page and nothing else"). The ADR owns it. Fix: keep the pointer, cut the restated clause.

## Gates run this session

- `nix flake check` -> all checks passed, but it reported \`running 0 flake checks\` with every derivation only "evaluated to", so that green proved nothing on its own.

title: Server SQLite backup timer
description:

Recovery for the index between rebuilds: a systemd timer in the server NixOS module running roughly hourly — sqlite3 .backup, zstd, aws s3 cp into a backups/ prefix in the same bucket, using the server's existing scoped credentials. Complements (does not replace) the rebuild-from-listing path.

Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.

title: NixOS VM end-to-end test
description:
## What to build

The one non-hermetic sanity gate (hydraJobs only, never in nix flake check): a NixOS VM test wiring a real idle Leios node (pinned via the ouroboros-leios prototype tag input, not capkgs), the real agent via its module, the real server via its module, and Garage as S3. Asserts the full path — scrape → spool → signed upload → verify → S3 object → ACK — once; moving values stay covered by tier-2 fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] VM test passes: an object appears in Garage and the agent logs the ACK.
- [ ] Runs from hydraJobs; excluded from nix flake check (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network).
- [ ] Leios pin is a flake input, bumpable with the fixture re-record flow.

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index; Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing .14 (NixOS VM end-to-end test). No untracked files; all six changed paths are staged except `.beads/issues.jsonl`.

## Correctness

- `nix/e2e-test.nix` (last subtest) — the comment "An empty archive verifies vacuously, so the count is the assertion" is false. `report_audit` (`crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:255`) returns `Fatal::ArchiveEmpty` on `(0, 0, 0)`, so `e2e.succeed` already fails on an empty bucket. Fix: drop the comment and the `re.search`, or keep the count and say what it actually adds.

## Prose

- `nix/e2e-test.nix` `nodeConfig` — "Converted to JSON (cardano-node's YAML parser reads JSON) so plain jq can address the empty-string TraceOptions key" is verbatim from `scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh` (its own `yq -o=json` block), and `devnet/flake.nix`'s `devnet-setup` states the same why a third time. Same for "No peers": three phrasings of one fact. Fix: a pointer, once the shared derivation lands (metsuke-4zo.60).
- `nix/e2e-test.nix` header and comments say "upload" and "batch" where `CONTEXT.md` §Submission reads "_Avoid_: upload, batch, post, payload". `upload_url` / `rate_limit_uploads` / the `'batch acked'` grep are schema and log strings and stay. The prose is new writing with nothing forcing the old spelling.

## Design call, your decision

`nix/e2e-test.nix` `poolId` — the constant is correct (checked: blake2b-224 of `poolKeys/cold.vkey`, bech32). Its comment argues a stale constant fails the ACK subtest rather than passing quietly, which holds. Against: `cardano-cli` is already in `leiosPkgs`, so a `runCommand` deriving it from `cold.vkey` would be self-correcting on a leios bump instead of failing CI. My recommendation is derive it — the failure mode the comment defends is a red CI run someone then has to diagnose.

## Verified, not findings

- `flake.nix` `leios-pin` reading `inputs.cardano-node-leios.rev` does not make `nix flake check` fetch anything it did not already fetch: `lazy-trees` is not in this Nix's `experimental-features`, so all locked inputs are realized during lock resolution regardless of use. The asymmetry with the devnet side's `importJSON` is style only.
- `devnet/flake.nix`'s `metsuke.url = "path:.."` evaluates with the devnet's gitignored `.devnet/node.socket` present (`nix eval --no-eval-cache .#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux.drvPath` succeeds).
- Both `wait_until_succeeds` greps are on specific log strings with `-q` on the final stage; neither passes vacuously.

## Gates run this session

- `nix flake check` — all checks passed (`running 0 flake checks`: every output already in the store).
- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.leios-pin` — built; both locks read `3534e7065419c906b35d3be7c976aeace8cf2085`.
- `nix eval .#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux.drvPath` (from `devnet/`) — evaluates.
- **The VM test itself was not run.** Acceptance criterion 1 ("an object appears in Garage and the agent logs the ACK") is unverified by this review; it needs `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` on a `/dev/kvm` host.

## Beads hygiene

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` is unstaged (` M`) and now carries this round's filings; `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code.
- .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason — pre-commit, your call.
- The map has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate. No `## Out of scope` line needed: nothing here crossed one.

Filed metsuke-4zo.86; commented on metsuke-4zo.60.

metsuke-4zo.87 (`needs-decision`) — `hydraJobs.e2e` is defined only in `devnet/flake.nix` and the repo carries no jobset config, so "runs from hydraJobs" holds only if CI is pointed at `devnet/` as a second flake. Jobset entry, or root re-export?

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All three round-1 fixes landed and are correct in substance; the prose axis is now clean (pointer to `scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh` resolves and does state the why for all three things it is cited for). Three findings, one design call, one proposed fix refuted.

## In-scope

- `crates/metsuke/tests/fixtures/README.md:6-10` — the re-record flow still reads "Re-record on every bump of the `cardano-node-leios` input in flake.nix". After this diff a bump also has to move `devnet/flake.lock` (or the new `leios-pin` check goes red) and re-check `poolId` (or the new first subtest goes red). This is acceptance criterion 3 — "Leios pin is a flake input, bumpable with the fixture re-record flow" — and the flow is now understated by two steps. Fix: name both in that bullet.
- `nix/e2e-test.nix`, first subtest — `assert derived == "${poolId}", derived` prints only what `cardano-cli` produced, never what it was compared against. The subtest exists to name a mismatch immediately, and its own failure message withholds half of it. Fix: `f"cardano-cli derived {derived}, expected ${poolId}"`.
- `nix/e2e-test.nix`, ACK subtest — `mc alias set` has no `--region` flag, so `mc` signs with `us-east-1` while Garage serves `garage`. From the run log: `Response: error 400 Bad Request, Authorization header malformed, unexpected scope: 20260825/us-east-1/s3/aws4_request`. The listing only comes back because `mc` re-signs after that error. The `region` binding's own comment says "the server signs against it, so the two have to be the same word" — `mc` is a third party that also has to and does not, and nothing here would notice if that retry went away. Fix: write the region into the alias config after `mc alias set`, or drop `mc` and assert the key prefix from something already region-correct.

## Design call, your decision

Two axes independently proposed moving the pool-id check from a guest subtest to a build-time `pkgs.runCommand`, shaped like `leios-pin`. Your IFD objection does not reach this shape: the derivation would compare `cardano-cli`'s output against the recorded constant and exit non-zero, never feeding a derived value back into evaluation, so nothing is imported from a derivation and `allow-import-from-derivation` stays irrelevant. Your second argument — that a recorded constant makes a changed `pool1` show up as a diff — is untouched either way, because the constant stays recorded under both. What changes is that the check runs without `/dev/kvm`, on any host, before a 4 GB VM boots, and stops the `cardano-cli` closure being installed in the guest for one string comparison. My recommendation is to move it. Keeping it is defensible: it is one subtest, it costs 9s, and it sits where a reader of the test finds it.

## Refuted, not a finding

Restoring an object-count assertion to the last subtest. The regex round 1 removed was `int(...) > 0`, not an exact count, so it never distinguished one stored object from several and adds nothing `succeed` does not already give. An exact count would be worse than nothing: in the run I inspected, `upload_interval_secs = 5` produced two PUTs and three `batch acked` lines before the units stopped, so the number of objects at verify time is a race.

## Gates run this session, on the working tree

- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → `/nix/store/q32lhl57hqjlyvm1fg7awg2301lkcsvy-vm-test-run-metsuke-e2e`. Read the log rather than trusting the exit code: all six subtests green, `metsuke[910]: batch acked` at t=19.6s, `v1/<poolId>/…json.zst` listed, `verify-archive` GETting the stored object. **Acceptance criterion 1 is met and is no longer unverified in this review.**
- `nix flake check` → all checks passed.
- Verified, not taken on report: `cardano-cli latest stake-pool id --output-bech32` exists in the pinned cli (11.1.0.0, `--output-bech32` is the default spelling), `cardano-cli` is on the guest PATH via `environment.systemPackages`, and its output matches the recorded constant exactly.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is still unstaged (` M`) and carries round 1's filings and both review comments — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason, which is yours to set. metsuke-4zo.86 and metsuke-4zo.87 stay as filed; .87 is still unanswered and your read (a second jobset entry for `devnet/`, not a root re-export) is not yet recorded on it.

Round-2 filings: none. All three findings above are this diff's own work.

Verdict: ready for /commit once the three in-scope items land. None changes behaviour, the VM test passes, and every gate is green.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 3. All three round-2 fixes landed and are correct; the `awscli2` swap is real (this round's log has zero `Authorization header malformed` lines and one clean `list-objects-v2`, against one 400-and-re-sign before). One blocking regression, one prose trim, two proposed findings refuted.

## Blocking

- `devnet/flake.nix` `flake.hydraJobs` — `nix flake check` in `devnet/` goes from exit 0 to exit 1. Nix evaluates every flake output with IFD enabled except `hydraJobs`, and reaching `cardano-node` through haskell.nix needs it: `error: cannot build '…-cardano-node-plan-to-nix-pkgs.drv^out' during evaluation because the option 'allow-import-from-derivation' is disabled`. Measured both sides in this session: a detached worktree at HEAD (`90cff82`, no `hydraJobs` in `devnet/flake.nix`) gives `all checks passed`, exit 0; the working tree fails while checking `hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux`. The root flake is unaffected — `hydraJobs.units` reaches only nixpkgs. This is acceptance criterion 2, "excluded from `nix flake check` (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network)": true of the root flake, and this diff makes it false of the devnet one. Options: expose the pair under `flake.legacyPackages.<system>`, which `nix flake check` does not force, and point the jobset there; or keep `hydraJobs` and state in `devnet/flake.nix` that its own flake check is expected red. The first keeps a green gate and is my recommendation; the second is cheaper but leaves a red gate in the repo, which is the thing that trains people to stop reading gates. It interacts with metsuke-4zo.87 — whatever CI is pointed at has to find the jobs — but it is a separate problem: .87 is jobset wiring, this is a gate that now fails.

## In-scope

- `nix/e2e-test.nix`, listing subtest — the comment about `mc` ("asks the bucket for its location, takes the 400 …, and re-signs — so it would list this bucket whether or not the region matched") narrates a tool that is no longer in this file, which is journey rather than why. It is also wrong about the contrast it draws: botocore performs the same redirect, retrying on `AuthorizationHeaderMalformed` when the error body carries a `Region` element, and Garage emits one — so `aws` would also list this bucket with a mismatched region. The comment claims coverage the assertion does not have. Fix: cut it. `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=${region}` next to the `region` binding needs no defence.

Optional, three words: the README's `` `checks.leios-pin` `` sits unqualified beside `` `hydraJobs.pool-id`, in the devnet flake ``. The parenthetical is correctly scoped to `pool-id` and `leios-pin` is in the root flake, so nothing is false — but the asymmetry invites the misread. "(`checks.leios-pin`, in the root flake)" closes it.

## Refuted, not findings

- `keyPrefix = "v1/"` as an unguarded Nix-side copy of `KEY_PREFIX` (`crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs:55`). Drift is caught, loudly: the listing is filtered by `--prefix ${keyPrefix}` and asserted to contain `${keyPrefix}${poolId}/`, so a `KEY_PREFIX` that moved in Rust alone puts the objects somewhere the filter does not reach and the assert fires. The comment is a pointer to the owner, not a second unchecked home, and needs no `runCommand`.
- Divergent Change in one file yielding two derivations with disjoint parameters. Splitting `poolIdRecorded` out would duplicate `devnetSrc`/`poolKeys`/`poolId` or make a second file import this one for three bindings. The header states the reason. Leave it.

## Verified, not taken on report

- `nix eval devnet#hydraJobs --apply attrNames` gives both `e2e` and `pool-id`, each with `x86_64-linux`: the `genAttrs`/`mapAttrs` shape is right and one jobset entry reaches both.
- `aws s3api … --query 'Contents[].Key' --output text` on a zero-match prefix prints `None` and exits 0, so `succeed` passes — but the assert still fires, with `None` as its message. Not a vacuous pass.
- `derived=$(cardano-cli …)` in `poolIdRecorded` is an assignment, not an argument-list substitution, so stdenv's `set -e` does see a `cardano-cli` failure. This is the shape metsuke-4zo.55 was about, on the right side of it.
- Both README red-on-drift claims hold: `checks.leios-pin` compares the two locks' `leios` revs, `hydraJobs.pool-id` compares the recorded `poolId` against the pinned tag's keys.

## Gates run this session

- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.pool-id.x86_64-linux devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → both built. Read the e2e log rather than the exit code: five subtests green, `batch acked` at t=20.0s, the `list-objects-v2` call clean, `verify-archive` GETting the stored object.
- `nix flake check` in the repo root → all checks passed.
- `nix flake check` in `devnet/` → **exit 1**, per the blocking finding above.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is still unstaged (` M`) — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code. Your read is recorded on metsuke-4zo.87 and it is correctly left open. metsuke-4zo.86 stays filed. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason, which is yours to set.

Round-3 filings: none. Both findings are this diff's own work.

Verdict: not ready for /commit — the devnet flake check regression is a gate this diff turns red, and the ticket's own second criterion is about exactly that.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 4. The `mc` comment is gone and both README qualifiers now resolve correctly. The flake-check regression is **not** fixed: your stated residual is right, and it is not a footnote — it is the finding.

## Blocking, carried from round 3

- `devnet/flake.nix:7` — `nixConfig.allow-import-from-derivation = true` is a no-op for anyone whose Nix does not already trust that setting, so `nix flake check` in `devnet/` still exits 1 off your machine. Measured this session with both `HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` pointed at a fresh directory, non-interactive:

  ```
  warning: ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting 'allow-import-from-derivation'.
  error: cannot build '…-cardano-node-plan-to-nix-pkgs.drv^out' during evaluation
         because the option 'allow-import-from-derivation' is disabled
  ```

  The rule, from `ConfigFile::apply` in libflake: a `nixConfig` key is applied if it is on a six-item whitelist (`bash-prompt*`, `flake-registry`, `commit-lock-file-summary`) — `allow-import-from-derivation` is not — else if `accept-flake-config = true`, else if `~/.local/share/nix/trusted-settings.json` holds that name and value, else it prompts, and a non-TTY prompt answers no. **`trusted-users` is never consulted on this path**, so being a trusted user does not help; on your machine it is the persisted `trusted-settings.json` entry doing the work, which is why the setting reads as unconditional from inside it.

  Your green measurement with and without `--accept-flake-config` is consistent with this and does not distinguish it: both runs read the same saved entry.

## What that leaves

The choice is now genuinely blocked on metsuke-4zo.87, because two of the three answers are CI-side. I have recorded this coupling there as a comment.

- **O1** — the pair under `flake.legacyPackages.<system>`, which `nix flake check` does not force, with a jobset that names the attribute. Green everywhere, no trust dependency. Costs the `hydraJobs` discovery convention, which is the objection you already raised and it stands.
- **O2** — keep `hydraJobs`, delete the `nixConfig`, and record in `devnet/flake.nix` that its own flake check is expected red. No trust dependency, honest, leaves a red gate.
- **O3** — keep both, and set `accept-flake-config = true` in the Hydra evaluator's own `nix.conf`. Keeps `hydraJobs` and every gate green, at the cost of a deployment-side fact this repo cannot assert.

My recommendation is **O3 if .87 resolves to a jobset you control**, since it is one line in the deployment and preserves the name the convention exists for; **O2 if it does not**, because a gate that is red for a stated reason is better than one that is green only where it was written. O1 remains available but pays the convention for a problem the other two solve.

Whichever you take, the `nixConfig` line as it stands is the one thing that should not survive unchanged: it currently makes the flake's evaluability depend on the reader's machine without saying so.

## Prose

- `devnet/flake.nix:4-6` — the comment presents the fix as unconditional. It states what `nix flake check` does and why IFD is needed, and never states the precondition that decides whether the line does anything. Fix falls out of the option chosen: under O3, say the evaluator must set `accept-flake-config`; under O2, the comment goes with the line.
- `devnet/flake.nix:5` — "`nix flake check` disables it by default" is Nix-internal behaviour with no version pin, sitting where nothing will report it stale. CLAUDE.md: a version pin claims the behaviour churns, so make it only when it does. Either pin it or state only the requirement and the error string.

Also, minor and falling out of the same decision: `nixConfig` is not scoped to `nix flake check`, so `nix build` and `nix develop` on `devnet/` prompt a first-time user too.

## Verified, not taken on report

- Root `nix flake check` → all checks passed; the root flake is genuinely untouched by the devnet `nixConfig`.
- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.pool-id.x86_64-linux devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → both built; the e2e log on the current derivation shows five subtests green and `batch acked` at t=19.2s. The `mc` comment is gone from the file.
- README: "(`checks.leios-pin`, in this flake)" resolves — the README sits in the root flake's tree and `leios-pin` is at `flake.nix:305` — and the sibling "(… in the devnet flake)" is correct for `pool-id`. The asymmetry is now the accurate one.
- `nixConfig`'s first sentence and the `inputs` comment below it state different facts (this flake needs IFD; haskell.nix is kept out of the root flake). Not a second copy.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` still unstaged — `git add .beads/` with the code. Comment added to metsuke-4zo.87 recording the trust coupling; it stays open and unanswered, and it now gates the choice above. metsuke-4zo.86 stays filed. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment.

Round-4 filings: none.

Verdict: not ready for /commit. One decision to make, and it is on .87.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 5. O3 is landed and works: both directions reproduce on a genuinely fresh trust store, and the "expected red" block is correctly gone. One clause of the new comment is false, measured.

## In-scope

- `devnet/flake.nix:6-7` — "an evaluator that already allows IFD never reads it" is wrong. Such an evaluator does read the line; acceptance and the evaluator's own IFD setting are independent gates. Measured on a fresh `HOME`/`XDG_DATA_HOME`, non-interactive, with `--option allow-import-from-derivation true` and no acceptance:

  ```
  warning: ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting 'allow-import-from-derivation'.
  all checks passed!
  ```

  The outcome half of the claim is right — the check passes, so the line is inert in effect — but the mechanism is not, and the observable consequence is that warning on every such evaluation, including Hydra's if its `nix.conf` allows IFD without setting `accept-flake-config`. Someone reading that warning in an evaluation log will go looking for a problem the comment told them could not exist.

  The clause is also the one O3 rests on, which is why it is worth correcting rather than cutting: what makes the setting inert on Hydra is that Hydra's own config already permits IFD, not that Hydra skips the line.

  Suggested wording, same length:

  ```
  # haskell.nix resolves cardano-node's plan by importing from a derivation, so
  # `nix flake check` — which refuses IFD — cannot evaluate the hydraJobs below
  # without this. Nix honours it only for a reader who has accepted this flake's
  # config; anyone else gets "ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting",
  # and then needs IFD allowed in their own nix.conf or the check fails.
  ```

## Verified this session

- Fresh `HOME`/`XDG_DATA_HOME`, non-interactive, no flag → `warning: ignoring untrusted flake configuration setting 'allow-import-from-derivation'` then `error: cannot build '…-cardano-node-plan-to-nix-pkgs.drv^out' … because the option 'allow-import-from-derivation' is disabled`.
- Same, with `--accept-flake-config` → both Hydra jobs checked, `all checks passed`.
- Same, with `--option allow-import-from-derivation true` and no acceptance → warning, then `all checks passed`. This is the third case the comment speaks to and the one it gets wrong.
- Both round-4 asks are met: the precondition is now stated rather than implied, and "which refuses IFD" is a statement about what `nix flake check` is for rather than an unpinned claim about a current default. It will not go stale the way "disables it by default" would have.
- The `nixConfig`, `inputs`, and `hydraJobs` comments state three different whys. Still not second copies.
- The deleted "expected red" block described a state that no longer exists; removing it was right.

## Gates run this session

- `nix flake check` in the repo root → all checks passed.
- `nix build devnet#hydraJobs.pool-id.x86_64-linux devnet#hydraJobs.e2e.x86_64-linux` → both built; the e2e log on the current derivation shows five subtests green and `batch acked` at t=19.2s.
- Devnet `nix flake check` in all three trust configurations above.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is still unstaged (` M`) and now carries five rounds of review comments and two filings — `git add .beads/` in the same commit as the code, or the record and the work part company. metsuke-4zo.87 holds the O3 answer and stays open on the jobset half, correctly scoped out of this ticket. metsuke-4zo.86 stays filed. .14 is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment or close reason.

Round-5 filings: none.

Verdict: ready for /commit once the one clause is corrected. Nothing about it changes behaviour, and every gate is green.

comments.text: Shipped: nix/e2e-test.nix, a single-machine NixOS VM test asserting scrape -> spool -> signed submission -> ACK -> object under v1/<poolId>/ -> verify-archive, on a real idle Leios node from the pinned proto-devnet config, the agent and server through their own modules, and Garage as S3.
