title: ADR 0007 rests on a mainnet premise that no longer holds
description:
docs/adr/0007 Context: "The agent may eventually run on mainnet block producers, so its privilege set is the attack surface." The project owner states there will be no mainnet in the foreseeable future.
The decision bars journal access and supplementary groups, which is exactly what the developers requested data needs. ADR 0007 already says widening is "a new decision that supersedes this one".
Fix: ADR 0010 supersedes it; CLAUDE.md invariant line 19 follows. Human decision, not an agent one.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Owner agrees the mainnet premise goes, and that the security goal does not. ADR 0010 must argue least privilege on its own terms, not treat the dead premise as licence.

Three ways to reach trace lines, narrowest first:
A. Node StandardOutput=append:<file>, metsuke ReadOnlyPaths that one path, DynamicUser survives. Narrowest, but replaces journal output so operators lose journalctl -u cardano-node, and node 11 has no file backend to tee with.
B. Pipe mode, metsuke as transparent tee. Zero privileges, journald keeps everything, but metsuke then runs inside the node unit alongside the KES and VRF keys.
C. SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal. Own unit, own hardening, no reach to node keys, dies without touching the node. Costs read of every unit's journal (journald has no per-unit ACL). No change to the node unit.

Recommendation: C, with the residual stated in Consequences and A named as the escape hatch.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: docs/adr/0010-log-based-trace-collection.md is drafted in the tree at status proposed, arguing the systemd-journal grant on least-privilege grounds with A/B/C compared. Remaining work is the owner's: accept it, flip ADR 0007's status, update CLAUDE.md's invariant line. .91 and .99 are blocked on that.

title: Pipe line source: cardano-node run | metsuke, for hosts without journald
description:
Not every SPO runs systemd/journald; docs/research/openblockperf.md:223 flags the same coupling. metsuke-4zo.91 covers the journald source only.
Same line-source abstraction, stdin as the second implementation. Requires no privileges and no ADR 0010 grant.
Transparent tee: every line read is written through to stdout unchanged, so the operator keeps whatever consumed the node output before.
Must ignore SIGPIPE and survive stdout write failure while still draining stdin. Dying on a closed downstream sends SIGPIPE to cardano-node and takes the block producer with it.
Must never block the node: drop when the spool is full rather than apply backpressure. EOF on stdin means the node exited, so flush and exit.
From the wire-rework spec (metsuke-jfb): the tee thread writes every line through to stdout FIRST, then enqueues on a bounded channel for a parse-and-spool worker. No JSON work ever sits on the node's write path. Drop on a full channel, matching the drop-when-full rule above. Blocked by metsuke-jfb.2 (parse-based selection) and metsuke-jfb.3 (per-line provenance).

title: Trace batch budget wedges permanently against the server decompress limit
description:
spool outstanding_rows budgets raw line bytes; server max_decompressed_bytes bounds serialized JSON. Lines pay string escaping samples never did: measured 1.1095x on the committed recording.
Both ship at 4194304. rows=12306 raw=4193975 -> json 4653395 -> rejected at decompress. 413 clamps backoff at upload_backoff_max_secs, the batch is deterministic, so the same batch retries daily forever and lines evict oldest-first after one warning.
Triggers at ~6h outage, or ~8min if namespaces is widened. contrib/config.example.toml tells the operator to set exactly the wedging value.
Fix: budget against serialized size, or ship upload_batch_max_bytes well under max_decompressed_bytes.
e2e never catches it: upload_interval_secs=5 never accumulates a full batch.
close_reason: Agent budgets against the bytes the server decompresses

comments.author: claude
comments.text: No second measure to disagree with: the row bytes column holds what the row costs in a sealed body, so the agent budgets against the bytes the server decompresses.

title: Instructions set the trace backend but never pin the node root severity
description:
Every Leios namespace is severity Info, below cardano-node default root threshold. The instructions page step sets only TraceOptions backends.
An SPO whose root severity sits above Notice emits no notice/warning traces either, metsuke selects nothing, and nothing reports it. "All error/warn/notice traces" silently returns a subset.
Fix: the page pins the root severity, not just the two Leios keys.
close_reason: Instructions page pins the node root severity

comments.author: claude
comments.text: The instructions page pins the node's root severity from the agent's own configured floor, checked by the_node_root_severity_comes_from_the_agents_own_floor.

title: Trace loss is invisible in the archive and removes contiguous time windows
description:
Four loss paths, none recorded in any archived object: spool eviction (logtail::drain reports the running total only when the drain ends, which under --follow is never), journald rate limiting, agent restart (--lines=0, no persisted cursor), and a wrong journal_unit that waits forever in silence.
All four remove a contiguous window, oldest-first, which skews a distribution rather than thinning it. The developers compute CDFs off these bytes and cannot tell a complete record from a truncated one.
Counter gaps reveal missing batches; nothing reveals missing lines.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Two more loss paths from reviewing the uncommitted tree, both invisible for the same reason:

- logsource::JournalSource::drop discards the child's exit status (let _ = kill/wait), so logtail's 'the trace line stream from <unit> ended' cannot distinguish journalctl refused the journal from a unit that does not resolve. Keep the wait status and put it in that warning.
- logselect::severity returns None for a spelling this build does not know, so a node that adds or renames a severity drops those lines from the floor rule with nothing counting them - the highest severities are exactly what the floor exists for. Either ship an unclassifiable line or count it in the drain report.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Third silent path in logtail::run, from the same tree: a JournalSource::spawn failure — journalctl_path wrong, binary absent, group grant missing — is eprintln'd and retried every respawn_backoff_secs forever. It is a startup config error the operator can fix, but start_trace_collection already returns Result<(), StartupError> and main already treats an unopenable spool as fatal, so this is the one such error that never reaches them. Fix: spawn once inside start_trace_collection, propagate as a StartupError, and keep the retry loop only for re-spawns of a stream that once worked.

title: Server pushes additional trace namespaces on ACK, bounded by local roots
description:
Node updates change namespaces; pushing config to every SPO to follow is coordination we do not want. Ack already carries latest_version (ADR 0006), so it is the established server-to-client channel.
Security bound is not optional: under ADR 0010 the agent holds systemd-journal and can read every unit journal on the host. The ns filter is the only thing scoping that. An unbounded server-pushed pattern turns a compromised ingest server into remote read of every SPO system journal.
Fix: local config sets namespace_roots; a pushed ns is accepted only if it is under one, otherwise refused and logged. severity_floor stays local.
Prefix match only. A regex arriving over the wire is a DoS primitive across the whole fleet.
Rules persist in the spool so a restart does not drop to bare config; local config is the floor when the server is unreachable. Needs an ADR: this changes who decides what an agent collects.

title: Extract wire contract into metsuke-wire crate
description: crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs is the wire contract; metsuke-server depends on the whole agent crate for it. Every future agent dep (HTTP, rusqlite, SNTP) becomes a server dep transitively, against least-privilege, and ADR 0006 independent versioning forces server manifest churn per client tag. Fix: move envelope.rs into a metsuke-wire crate both binaries depend on. Deliberately deferred from metsuke-4zo.1 review: do it when the first heavy agent dependency lands (metsuke-4zo.2/.4).
close_reason: wire contract extracted to metsuke-wire; server off the agent crate

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Trigger fired: metsuke-4zo.2 added ureq (+ its tree) to the metsuke lib, so metsuke-server now pulls it transitively. Extraction is due.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Trigger fired: rusqlite (bundled sqlite) landed in metsuke via metsuke-4zo.4, so metsuke-server now links it transitively. Review of .4 endorses the wire-crate option over a feature gate.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
More cross-crate duplication for the extraction to absorb, found reviewing metsuke-4zo.16:

- journald severity prefixes: crates/metsuke/src/main.rs ERR/WARNING/INFO (private) vs crates/metsuke-server/src/lib.rs ERR/WARNING/INFO — byte-identical.
- lowercase hex encode: metsuke/src/uploader.rs `fn hex` (private) vs metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs `fn hex` — byte-identical.
- hex decode, three shapes: metsuke/src/keys.rs `decode_seed`, metsuke/tests/support/mod.rs `decode_hex`, metsuke-server/src/http.rs `decode_hex<const N>` (the best-shaped of the three).
- `Args::parse` loop: metsuke/src/cli.rs vs metsuke-server/src/cli.rs — same shape; the client's `value()` helper already generalises the flag-value case.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree. No untracked files; everything is staged. Gate: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{test,clippy,treefmt,deny,audit}` all built green.

## Intent

Extraction itself is complete and correct. metsuke-server no longer depends on metsuke; envelope.rs and sqlite.rs moved byte-identical; journal prefixes and hex are unified. build.rs matches ADR 0006 ("the client crate's version read from the workspace at server compile time") and tests/version.rs guards it.

- crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs:282-299 — hex()/unhex() were not folded into metsuke_wire::hex, so the tree ships two hex decoders with different strictness: unhex() has no is_ascii_hexdigit pre-check, so u8::from_str_radix accepts a '+' pair ("+f" -> 15) that hex::decode rejects. Also s3.rs:285 'Mirrors the header decoder in `http`' is now false — http.rs delegates. Fix: hex::encode at s3.rs:164-165, hex::decode::<N> at s3.rs:258-260 mapping HexError into the local String refusal, delete both fns. Tracked in metsuke-4zo.23, commented there.
- cli.rs value() dedup, named in comment 3 of this ticket, is untouched. Already metsuke-4zo.23's, commented.

## Standards

- CLAUDE.md:24 — "`crates/metsuke-wire` is what the two agree on, and the only crate either depends on" is false. metsuke-server declares 10 other direct deps (rusqlite, rusty-s3, serde, serde_json, thiserror, time, tiny_http, toml, ureq, url) plus a toml build-dep; metsuke declares 7. Fix: drop the second clause.
- metsuke-wire holds journal.rs and sqlite.rs, neither of which is anything the two sides agree on over the wire, and pulls rusqlite bundled. No leak (the server links rusqlite directly anyway), but the crate's name and its lib.rs header both claim narrower than its contents. Fix: reword, or split. Reword is the recommendation.

## Silent failures

- crates/metsuke/src/keys.rs:75 — `hex::decode::<32>(digits).ok()` throws away HexError::WrongLength{found, expected}, which hex.rs was written to carry, so a truncated key file reports NotAnEd25519Seed with no byte count. Fix: `#[source] HexError` on the variant and map_err instead of .ok().

## Prose

- crates/metsuke-server/build.rs:1-2 — first sentence narrates what main() does. Drop it, keep the ADR-0006 clause.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs:79-80 — the new doc says only what the four-line match does, replacing a doc that carried a real why (the uppercase-accepted rationale, which correctly moved to hex.rs). Fix: state why the wrapper exists (HexError doesn't know which header) or delete.
- The dependency-leak why appears three times: metsuke-wire/src/lib.rs:1-4 (owner), CLAUDE.md:24, build.rs:3-4. Cut the other two to pointers.
- crates/metsuke-wire/src/hex.rs:1 'Hex for the upload headers' — keys.rs now decodes a cardano-cli seed through it, which is not a header.

## Discarded

build.rs and tests/version.rs both parsing ../metsuke/Cargo.toml is the point of the test, not duplication. flake.nix version="0" is crane derivation naming only, no ADR 0006 conflict.

## Verdict

Not ready: 7 in-scope fixes above, none structural. Also `git add .beads/` — this review's comments dirtied issues.jsonl.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. Gate re-run this session: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{test,clippy,treefmt,deny,audit}` -> exit 0.

All seven round-1 fixes verified in the tree. The keys.rs split plus its three new tests is a better outcome than what I asked for — the malformed-seed path had no coverage at all. Keeping `unhex` as a message adapter is right; it now mirrors `number` beside it.

Two findings, both from round 1's own edits.

- crates/metsuke-server/src/s3.rs:283 — the rewrite dropped `{text:?}`, so a refusal no longer says what it got: `"{header} is not {N} bytes of hex: {error}"` against the old `{text:?}`. CLAUDE.md ## Code: 'a message naming what failed and what it got'. The length case also states the expectation twice ('is not 32 bytes of hex: decodes to 31 bytes, expected 32'), since HexError already carries it. Fix: `format!("{header} is not hex: {error} ({text:?})")`.
- metsuke-4zo.39 carries `to-issues:build`, but its title is 'Decide whether…' and its body recommends wont-do. That label puts it on the implement frontier, where the next agent builds the thing the ticket argues against. Fix: relabel `needs-decision`.

On the cli.rs deferral: accepted, no overrule. Two grammars and two ArgsError shapes reduce the shared part to one stdlib call, and a wire module around it deletes no logic.

Verdict: one code fix (s3.rs message) and one label change. Nothing structural.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Extracted crates/metsuke-wire (envelope, sqlite, hex, journal); metsuke-server no longer depends on metsuke. Server reads the agent version via build.rs + CLIENT_VERSION per ADR 0006, cross-checked by tests/version.rs. Shared hex replaced four copies and tightened decode (from_str_radix accepted a sign pair). cli.rs value() dedup declined and closed as metsuke-4zo.39.

title: Slow request body stalls all ingest
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs: serve() reads bodies on the accepting thread and tiny_http 0.12 exposes no socket timeout (ServerConfig is addr+ssl only; Request hands out no stream), so one client trickling a body blocks every pool until it gives up. read_body bounds size, not time.

Fix: front the server with a proxy that fully buffers request bodies, and bind loopback. Belongs with metsuke-4zo.12, which owns the NixOS modules and the hardened unit. If the endpoint is ever exposed directly, tiny_http has to go.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Same root cause, second cost: memory, not just time.

Any path that answers without reading the body (413 by Content-Length, 404, 405, header-decode 400) leaves the remainder unread, and tiny_http's EqualReader::drop drains it with a single `vec![0; remaining]` sized by the *declared* Content-Length (util/equal_reader.rs:66-85; the >1024 branch at request.rs:215). Request::drop runs it on the serving thread, and no public Request method lets you skip it (upgrade/into_writer/respond all drop self).

Measured, debug build, one header-only POST declaring Content-Length: 4000000000, answered 400: VmSize 347544 kB -> 4253796 kB, freed when the client closed. RSS stays ~4 MB (calloc zero pages) until the attacker actually sends bytes.

Consequence: under the hardened unit's MemoryMax/LimitAS (metsuke-4zo.12) this aborts the process. Fix is the same proxy body cap this ticket already names; the cap has to be enforced *before* the request reaches tiny_http.

title: Agent panics on an https upload URL: ureq has no TLS provider
description:
crates/metsuke/Cargo.toml pins ureq with default-features = false, so no TLS feature is on: cargo tree -p metsuke -e features shows no rustls. ureq 3.4.0 panics on an https URI when the provider feature is off (ureq-3.4.0/src/unversioned/transport/mod.rs:485, "uri scheme is https ... feature is not enabled"). TLS is a hard requirement (docs/research/endpoint-protection.md, Transport).

Masked in the workspace: metsuke-server now takes ureq with defaults, and feature unification hands the agent rustls whenever both crates build together. An agent-only static build (metsuke-4zo.12) would not get it.

Fix: enable rustls on the agent ureq too, or bound the upload URL to https at config load and fail loudly there.
close_reason: agent ureq carries rustls; test-agent gate guards it

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Review of the uncommitted tree implementing metsuke-b4r. Three files, all staged, no untracked files.

## The ticket's own premise is wrong, and the diff's comment is right

metsuke-b4r says ureq 3.4.0 *panics* on an https URI with no provider feature. It does not, in this configuration. `WarnOnMissingTlsProvider` is chained only under `#[cfg(feature = "_tls")]` (ureq-3.4.0/src/unversioned/transport/mod.rs:381-395), and `_tls` arrives only via `rustls-no-provider` or `native-tls-no-default`, neither of which `default-features = false` turns on. `TcpConnector` opens a plain socket, then run.rs:404-407 returns `Error::TlsRequired`, which uploader.rs:45 maps to `Retryable`. Observed directly: run at HEAD, the new test sees a TCP connection carrying zero bytes and no panic.

So the Cargo.toml comment is accurate as written and needs no change. What needs correcting is the ticket body, in the resolution comment.

The fix itself is verified: `cargo tree -p metsuke -e features` now shows rustls + ring + webpki-roots.

## In-scope fixes

- `crates/metsuke/tests/uploader.rs:117-118` — the test does not guard the regression under this repo's gate, so the claim "the agent's transport carries a provider, not just the workspace build's" is held by nothing. `checks.test` is `craneLib.cargoTest commonArgs` (flake.nix:136) with no `-p`, so ureq's features unify across the workspace and metsuke-server's bare `ureq = "3.4.0"` supplies rustls either way. Measured at HEAD with this test file and the *old* Cargo.toml: `cargo test --workspace --test uploader an_https_upload_url_speaks_tls` → ok; `cargo test -p metsuke --test uploader …` → FAILED, `peer saw ""`. Fix: add a `cargoTest` check with `cargoExtraArgs = "--package metsuke"` (flake.nix:105 already builds the agent alone, but line 88 disables its tests), or drop the clause and let the manifest line hold the claim alone.
- `tests/uploader.rs:126,131` — `accept()` and `read()` are unbounded, and `join()` after them. Not a hang today, because ureq opens TCP before answering `TlsRequired` (0.01s failure, above). It becomes one the moment metsuke-4zo.40 lands: rejecting a non-https scheme at config load means `upload` returns before connecting, `accept()` blocks forever, and `cargo test` has no per-test timeout. Fix: `listener.set_nonblocking(true)` polled to a deadline, or run `upload` in the spawned thread and accept with a timeout, returning an empty vec so the existing assert reports it.
- `tests/uploader.rs:141` — `let _ = upload(...)` discards the outcome while the comment above it claims "the outcome is a transport failure either way". Nothing checks that, so the test also passes on `Acked`. Fix: bind it and assert `matches!(outcome, UploadOutcome::Retryable(_))`. That also turns the hang above into a fast, self-describing failure.
- `tests/uploader.rs:126-134` — third hand-rolled `UploadConfig`, alongside `upload_config(&MockServer)` at `:50` and the copy at `:101-105`. Same pool_id derivation, same 5s timeout. Fix: `fn upload_config(base: &str, timeout: Duration)`, callers pass `&server.uri()` or the https literal.
- `tests/uploader.rs:127-129` — the 5-byte buffer is pretence: only `bytes.first()` is asserted, so a 1-byte read passes and a 0-byte read yields an empty diagnostic string. Fix: `read_exact` on one byte, or assert the whole record header.

Optional prose trims, lower value: `Cargo.toml:18` "the upload endpoint is https" is a third copy — `contrib/config.example.toml` owns the value, `docs/research/endpoint-protection.md` §Transport owns the why; and `0x16` at `tests/uploader.rs:144` would be better as a named const than a comment.

## Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged with the code, and it matches after a flush. metsuke-b4r is still `in_progress` with no resolution comment and no close reason — pre-commit, your call. metsuke-4zo has no `## Decisions so far` or `## Not yet specified` section, so nothing to graduate. The new metsuke-4zo.40 in the diff is correctly parented and labelled.

## Gates, all run in this session

`nix flake check` → all checks passed. `cargo test --workspace` → 0 failed. `cargo test -p metsuke` → 0 failed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- --deny warnings` → silent. `cargo fmt --all --check` → clean.

## Filed

Filed metsuke-4zo.41.

Verdict: ready for /commit on correctness — the Cargo.toml fix is right and every gate is green. The one item worth doing first is the gate gap: as it stands the new test would not catch this regression coming back.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Premise correction: ureq 3.4.0 does not panic here. WarnOnMissingTlsProvider is chained only under cfg(feature = "_tls"), which default-features = false also turns off, so the observed behaviour is Error::TlsRequired, which uploader.rs reads as Retryable — an agent-only build retries an https URL forever instead of failing loudly.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Round 2. All five round-1 in-scope fixes landed. The gate gap is genuinely closed — verified end to end, not taken on report — and the remaining findings are all in the new test's diagnostics.

## The gate now catches the regression

Built a probe worktree carrying this round's `flake.nix` and `tests/uploader.rs` with `features = ["rustls"]` removed, committed so nix would see it, and ran `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.test-agent`: the derivation **fails**, `an_https_upload_url_speaks_tls ... FAILED`, in 0.02s. The cargoArtifacts-masking worry from round 1 does not apply — cargo fingerprints a unit on its feature set, so `--package metsuke` recompiles ureq as a distinct unit regardless of what the workspace deps build warmed. On the real tree the same check passes with the test present (`test an_https_upload_url_speaks_tls ... ok` in its log).

## In-scope fixes

- `tests/uploader.rs:146,162` — the gate's failure message is false in exactly the case the gate exists for. `read_exact(...).ok()` maps a short read to `None`, and the call site reports `.expect("nothing reached the listener")`. But a connection *does* arrive: ureq's `TcpConnector` opens the socket, then answers `TlsRequired`, so the peer sees a connection carrying zero bytes. Observed in the probe build above — that is the literal message the broken gate printed. Round 1 asked for the opposite ("a 0-byte read yields an empty diagnostic string"). The `opening_bytes` docstring at `:120-121` ("`None` if nothing connects") is wrong for the same reason, and a 1-to-4-byte cleartext regression reports "nothing reached the listener" too. Fix: `let n = stream.read(&mut buffer).unwrap_or(0);` returning `Option<Vec<u8>>`, assert on `bytes.get(..2)`; the existing `from_utf8_lossy` then prints what actually arrived. Reserve `None` for the accept deadline alone, and panic with the io error on a read that fails.
- `tests/uploader.rs:102-104` — the comment now describes a URL that moved out from under it:

      // TEST-NET-1 (RFC 5737) is unroutable: connect fails, nothing answers.
      timeout: Duration::from_millis(200),
      ..upload_config("http://192.0.2.1:9")

  Fix: put it above the `..upload_config(...)` line, or above the whole `UploadConfig {`.
- `tests/uploader.rs:124` — `deadline` is a `Duration`, and a deadline is an instant. The doc comment's "within `deadline`" and the arithmetic `deadline.saturating_sub(start.elapsed())` at `:143` both read as a budget. Fix: `within` or `budget`.
- `tests/uploader.rs:149-150` — third copy of the feature-unification why. `flake.nix:138-140` now owns it, because that comment is the only one justifying why `test-agent` exists; the metsuke-b4r body is the second and `crates/metsuke-wire/Cargo.toml:19-20` is a different fact (why wire declares no TLS) and stays. - `tests/uploader.rs:122-123` and `:169-170` — the dropped-connection why twice in one file, 47 lines apart. The comment at the assert owns it; drop the clause from the `opening_bytes` docstring.
- `tests/uploader.rs:116` — "A TLS record header" sits over a `[u8; 2]`, and it is the first two of five. `TLS_HANDSHAKE_PREFIX` already says handshake, so only `0x03` is non-derivable. Fix: "First two bytes of a TLS record header: handshake, then the legacy record version's major byte." The `0x03` claim itself is correct and stable — RFC 8446 §5.1 pins legacy_record_version to 0x0301 or 0x0303, and every TLS 1.0-1.2 record version is 0x03xx.

Low, mechanism verified but near-unreachable: `tests/uploader.rs:143` — if `accept()` lands after the budget has elapsed, `saturating_sub` gives zero, and `set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::ZERO))` returns `Err(InvalidInput, "cannot set a 0 duration timeout")` (confirmed on rustc 1.97.1), so the `.unwrap()` panics with an unrelated message. `.max(Duration::from_millis(1))` closes it.

title: Wire format rework and server simplification
description:
Rebuild the wire format as a zstd skippable-frame container (self-describing, duckdb-readable) and
strip the server to a stateless pipe: allowlist, cold-key verify, PUT. Fixes multi-machine data loss
(replay refusal, key collisions), removes Calidus/db-sync/SQLite, swaps tiny_http for hyper. Spec
was ephemeral; the durable record is the code.

## Decisions so far

- The container is a skippable frame (0x184D2A50, u32le length, plaintext JSON header) then a zstd
  data frame of JSON Lines, one detached Ed25519 signature over both. Header reads with no key and
  no decompressor. Both crates switched at once — no compatibility story, the bucket does not exist
  yet (jfb.1).
- max_header_bytes is a required [ingest] field, not a defaulted one: config.rs takes no defaults
  (jfb.1).
- Trace-line selection parses the line and reads the object's top level, rather than scanning for
  "ns":" and "sev":". The substring readers needed a first-occurrence and a last-occurrence rule,
  which was an unenforced claim about the node's key order. Every line the parse refuses declares
  neither field and is not selected; the distinct failures are one bucket. ADR 0010 amended
  (jfb.2).
- agent_id is a Header field, so identity on the wire is pool plus machine. jfb.4 keys objects by
  both, and a per-agent sequence number only reads if the header says which agent counted (jfb.3).
- A spooled row this build cannot read back is deleted and reported, not propagated: the parse
  refuses it every tick, so failing the tick stalls the stream behind one row until the byte cap
  catches up. Same trade as the over-budget head row (jfb.3).

title: Wire container: skippable-frame header + zstd data frame, both crates switched
description:
## What to build

A submission becomes exactly one zstd skippable frame (magic 0x184D2A50, u32le length, JSON header) followed by one zstd data frame (compressed JSON Lines), with a single detached Ed25519 signature over the whole byte sequence, verified with verify_strict. Header fields: schema version, pool id, agent id, agent version, sequence number, timestamp. The header is readable by seeking 8 bytes in with no decompressor; every conforming zstd tool (incl. duckdb read_json_auto) ignores the skippable frame and reads the payload — verified duckdb v1.5.2 / zstd 1.5.7 during design.

Both the agent (seal) and server (open) switch in this one ticket, because there is no compatibility story — the bucket does not exist yet. Existing server gates (replay, skew, schema) keep operating off the new header fields so CI stays green; their removal is a later ticket.

Header length is bounded by a max_header_bytes configuration value, default 4 KiB. A body not beginning with the skippable-frame magic, or declaring a header longer than the bound, is refused with 400 before anything else happens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Seal produces a byte sequence whose first frame is a skippable frame with the expected magic and length
- [ ] Open recovers the header without decompressing (seek 8 bytes, no zstd)
- [ ] A mutated byte anywhere in the file fails verification
- [ ] A body without the magic is refused; a header exceeding the bound is refused
- [ ] max_header_bytes is configuration, surfaced as a NixOS module option
- [ ] Committed fixture produced by the real sealing path, plus a test shelling out to `zstd -d` asserting it emits exactly the payload (recording, not assertion; re-record to detect drift)
- [ ] Agent seals the new container; server opens it; e2e VM test stays green

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: Skippable-frame header plus zstd data frame, both crates switched

comments.text:
## Review

Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` — 0 failures across all targets, incl. `zstd_decompresses_the_recordings_to_exactly_their_payloads`, `this_build_seals_the_recorded_submissions`, `every_submission_begins_with_a_skippable_frame`, `the_header_reads_back_without_a_decompressor`, `tampered_byte_rejects`. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — clean. The e2e VM test was NOT run.

Nothing untracked; the whole change is staged.

### Intent
- docs/adr/0001-raw-ed25519-detached-signature.md:1,17 — title and Decision still say the client signs "the zstd-compressed request body"; the signed bytes are now a skippable frame (plaintext JSON) plus a data frame. envelope.rs:3 cites ADR 0001 for a layout it no longer describes, and CLAUDE.md's invariant line repeats the stale wording. Fix: amend the Decision to name the container, update the CLAUDE.md line.
- Header carries five of the six fields the spec listed; `agent_id` is absent repo-wide. Raised on metsuke-jfb.3, which owns agent identity.
- Ticket says `max_header_bytes` has "default 4 KiB"; config.rs's own rule is "a missing limit is a deployment mistake, not a value to guess", and the field shipped as required `NonZeroU64`. Implementation is right, ticket wording is stale.

### Silent failures
- crates/metsuke-server/src/authority.rs:164-166 — the comment says "the ingest path refuses a malformed container before it gets here", but verify.rs:66 calls `authenticate` directly with no prior `split`, so a corrupted S3 object reaches this arm through the audit path. Fix: say the arm serves the audit path, which has no upstream container check.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/authority.rs:167 — the wildcard `error =>` replaced an exhaustive match over `OpenError`. Behaviour is unchanged today, but a future variant compiles silently into `MalformedPayload` with no compiler nudge. Fix: list `Container`, `Decompress`, `Json`, `NotUtf8`, `UnterminatedLine` as explicit arms.

### Standards
- crates/metsuke/tests/{agent,binary,delivery,logtail,uploader}.rs — `TEST_LIMITS` is the same literal five times; tests/support/mod.rs exists for exactly this and already holds `test_key`. Fix: move it there.

### Prose
- contrib/config.example.toml:41-42 — "It also covers the header, which the server bounds separately, so a batch under it is under both" does not follow: a submission under `upload_batch_max_bytes` can still exceed `max_header_bytes`. Fix: drop the clause, or say the agent does not bound the header against the server's header limit.
- nix/e2e-test.nix:88-94 — the offsets 4, 8, and `+9` are hardcoded in shell, duplicating `envelope::HEADER_OFFSET`. Nothing keeps them in sync across the language boundary. Fix: note the coupling to `HEADER_OFFSET` in the comment.

### Tests
- crates/metsuke-wire/tests/envelope.rs:69 — `arb_agent_version` narrowed `any::<String>()` to `[0-9a-zA-Z.+-]{0,32}`. The header bound justifies the length cap, not dropping quotes, control chars, and non-ASCII, which was the JSON-escaping coverage. Fix: `".{0,32}"`.

Filed nothing new; commented on metsuke-jfb.3.

## Review, round 2

Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` — 0 failures. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — clean. `cargo fmt --all --check` — exit 0. I did not re-run `nix flake check` or the e2e VM build; taking the author's report on those.

All seven round-1 fixes verified correct and complete in themselves. Checked specifically: `OpenError` has eight variants, three handled above the new arm and five listed in it, no wildcard and no `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a new variant fails the build (authority.rs:153-177). `verify::verify` at verify.rs:66 does call `authenticate` with no upstream `split`, so the corrected comment holds. `TEST_LIMITS` values are identical to all five removed copies. `"(?s).{0,32}"` cannot overflow the 4096-byte bound: 32 scalar values escape to at most 6 bytes each, 192 worst case.

Three doc comments still say the signed bytes are "the compressed body". That was true before this diff and is not now — the body is a plaintext-JSON skippable frame plus the compressed data frame, which is exactly what the reworded ADR 0001 Decision now says. This diff made them stale:

- crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs:194 — `/// Cap on the compressed body.` on `max_body_bytes`, which now caps header frame plus data frame
- crates/metsuke-server/tests/intake.rs:295 — `// The compressed body is capped before anything touches it.`

Fix: say "the wire body" or "the body as sent" at all three, matching the ADR's wording.

Container shipped: skippable frame (0x184D2A50, u32le length, plaintext JSON header) then a zstd data frame of JSON Lines, one detached Ed25519 signature over both. envelope::split reads the header with no key and no decompressor; open verifies, splits, parses, then inflates only the data frame. body() replaced by header_json()/payload_lines(); samples moved into the data frame as one object per line, which deleted OpenError::BodyContradictsVersion.

max_header_bytes is a required [ingest] field (NixOS option, 4096 in the example); IngestConfig::limits() pairs it with max_decompressed_bytes as envelope::Limits through authenticate/verify/audit. The container check is the first check in Intake::submit, before allowlist, limiter and cryptography, as Rejection::NotASubmission -> 400.

Fixtures submission-samples.hex and submission-lines.hex recorded by scripts/record-submission.sh; two tests over both, reseal-to-recorded-bytes and 'zstd -d emits exactly the payload'. v1 recording and its recorder deleted, no compatibility story.

Deferred: agent_id to jfb.3 (owns the config field, hostname slugification, provenance); the counter -> sequence rename to jfb.5 (owns the CONTEXT.md term). Ticket's 'default 4 KiB' wording is stale: config.rs takes no defaults, so the field is required.

title: logselect: unknown severity spelling silently reads as no severity
description: logselect.rs reads severity via read("sev").and_then(|name| name.parse().ok()) — a spelling outside the known ladder becomes None, so the line dodges every severity rule with no signal. Same class of unenforced node-output claim ADR 0010's parse rework removed for key order; a node version renaming a severity silently changes selection. Fix: count refusals and warn once per unknown spelling (like the cap-drop report), selection unchanged. Predates metsuke-jfb.3; found in its review.

title: Spool::readable can drain the whole spool if a reader regresses
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs, `Spool::readable`: an unreadable row is deleted and counted, with no bound on how many one tick may delete.

The accepted trade (metsuke-jfb.3) covers one bad row. It does not cover a regression in `Sample`/`TraceLine` deserialization, where every row refuses and every tick deletes everything it reads — ADR 0004 makes the spool the only durability layer, and the operator gets one stderr line naming the last row.

Q: bound it (delete at most N unreadable rows per tick, return the error past the bound so a systematic break stops the agent) or accept the unbounded drain and say so at the site?

title: logselect drops a node line that carries a metsuke key with no trace of it
description:
crates/metsuke/src/logselect.rs, `select`: `let Ok(line) = TraceLine::parse(line) else { return Selection::Skip }` discards the refusal.

`TraceLineError::ReservedKey` is not malformation — it is a well-formed node line whose top level happens to hold `metsuke`. jfb.2 put malformed lines in one bucket; this one is silent data loss with no counter and no log.

Fix: count `ReservedKey` refusals separately and surface them the way `UncarriableReport` is surfaced.

title: Envelope and Header should hold a Provenance field, not four loose ones
description:
crates/metsuke-wire/src/envelope.rs: `pool_id`, `agent_id`, `counter`, `timestamp` travel together through `Envelope`, `Header` and `Provenance`, and `Header::of` copies them field by field into a fourth place.

`Envelope::new` is six positional args; adding `agent_id` forced edits at ~15 call sites across both crates and every test support module.

Fix: `Envelope { provenance, agent_version, payload }`, so `Header::provenance` is a field read and the `agent_version` clone in `Header::of` goes.

title: CONTEXT.md has no Agent term, and the diff names the concept four ways
description:
CONTEXT.md defines no Agent or Agent ID entry, while `AgentId` is now a wire field stamped on every archived line.

New prose names the same thing "machine" (contrib/config.example.toml, delivery.rs), "agent" (identity.rs), "host" (identity.rs), "relay" (fixtures). CONTEXT.md Relationships still implies a Pool reports once.

Fix: add Agent and Agent ID under Reporting with an Avoid list picking one of machine/host, plus "a Pool may report from many Agents".

title: push_capped runs the eviction sweep on every single row push
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs, `push_capped` (pre-existing): the window-function `DELETE ... WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT ... SUM(bytes) OVER ...)` scans the whole table on every push, whether or not the table is anywhere near `max_bytes`, and both SQL strings are re-formatted and re-prepared each call.

This is the per-trace-line hot path.

Fix: `Connection::prepare_cached` for both statements, and gate the sweep on the table total exceeding `max_bytes`.

title: Trace lines parsed as JSON; filter reads parsed fields
description:
## What to build

Trace lines are parsed as JSON objects. This replaces the current substring matching on `"ns":"` and `"sev":"` and its hand-reasoned first-occurrence and last-occurrence rules — the namespace/severity filter reads parsed fields instead. A line that does not parse has no namespace and no severity, so no filter matches it and it is not selected. No special case, no counter, no reporting for unparseable lines (explicitly YAGNI).

Filtering happens after parsing. If trace volume on a real block producer makes that cost something, a cheap prefilter is a local change later — measure on the devnet before optimising.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing log-selection cases pass against parsed fields rather than substrings
- [ ] The nested-ns-inside-data case that motivated the first/last-occurrence rules is trivially correct and stays as a test
- [ ] An unparseable line matches no filter and is not selected

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: Trace lines parsed as JSON; the filter reads the object's top-level ns and sev

## Review

Gates run this session: `cargo test --workspace` — 0 failures across all targets, incl. the six rewritten logselect cases. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — clean. `cargo fmt --all --check` — exit 0. `nix flake check` and the e2e VM build were NOT run.

Nothing untracked; the whole change is staged.

### Intent
All three acceptance criteria met. Substring readers gone (`Fields::of`), nested-ns-in-data kept as `a_namespace_nested_in_data_is_not_the_lines_namespace`, unparseable line covered by `a_truncated_line_declares_nothing_and_is_not_selected`. No unasked behaviour.

### Prose
- crates/metsuke/src/logselect.rs:121-123 — the `Fields` doc restates the body ("declares neither" is the `else => Fields::default()` arm; "a severity this build cannot spell is not declared" is `.parse().ok()`), and the one claim that is not restatement is narrower than the behaviour: a line that *is* a JSON object but spells `ns` as a non-string also deserializes to `Fields::default()`, losing a well-formed `sev` with it. Fix: cut to what the code cannot say — that the two fields are read off the object's own top level, and any deserialize failure is one bucket.

### Efficiency
- crates/metsuke/src/logselect.rs:116-118 — `Keys` holds `Option<String>`, so every parsed line heap-allocates twice, including the majority the rules drop. The substring readers allocated nothing. This is not the parse cost the ADR bullet defers; it is avoidable within the chosen approach. Fix: `#[serde(borrow)] ns: Option<Cow<'a, str>>` (`Cow`, not `&str` — a value carrying an escape cannot borrow), lifetime through `Fields`.

### Beads
Ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason; the map metsuke-jfb has no `## Decisions so far` section. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is in sync and staged, carrying only the in_progress flip.

Filed nothing.

comments.text:
Selection parses the line instead of scanning it. logselect::Fields { namespace, severity } is built
by Fields::of, which deserializes the top level into a private Keys; the NS/SEV constants, string_at,
and the free namespace()/severity() functions are gone, and with them the first-occurrence and
last-occurrence rules — those were an unenforced claim about the node's key order. Every line the
parse refuses lands in one bucket declaring neither field, so no rule matches it: not an object, ns
not a string, cut short. No counter, no reporting (ticket's YAGNI).

Fields borrows out of the line. The fields go through a transparent newtype Read<'a>(Cow<'a, str>)
because #[serde(borrow)] does not reach through an Option — on Option<Cow<'a, str>> the attribute
compiles and every value still arrives owned, verified in a scratch crate. A borrowed &'a str field
would have refused any escaped value outright, dropping the whole line.

Tests: the_string_rules_read_what_a_json_parse_reads is gone (it compared a parse against a parse)
and four replace it — a_namespace_nested_in_data_is_not_the_lines_namespace,
a_truncated_line_declares_nothing_and_is_not_selected (real recorded line cut at its last comma,
both fields still present), every_recorded_record_declares_the_fields_a_rule_reads, and
reading_a_field_copies_only_what_the_line_does_not_spell_literally, which pins Borrowed for the
recorded shape and Owned for a .-escaped one. Cow's PartialEq compares contents, so the variant
needs matches!, not assert_eq!.

ADR 0010 amended: the Decision said "as substrings rather than by decoding the line". New
Consequences bullet records that the parse costs every line the node writes, that nobody has
measured it on a real block producer, and that a prefilter ahead of it is a local change.

title: Agent identity: agent id, per-line provenance, pool-id startup check
description:
## What to build

Every machine identifies itself. A new agent-id configuration field defaults to the slugified hostname — slugify rather than reject, since a machine that will not start over an underscore in its hostname is data loss for no benefit. The resolved id is logged at startup.

Every payload line — metrics and trace alike — carries the header fields (pool, agent, sequence number, timestamp) nested under the single reserved key `metsuke`. A metrics line is the sample fields plus `metsuke`; a trace line is the node's parsed JSON object plus `metsuke`. Nesting rather than flat merge: cardano-node's top-level trace keys are node-version-defined, and one reserved key is a constraint statable in a sentence. Measured overhead: +3.4% compressed.

The sequence number stays persisted before sealing, unchanged mechanically; its meaning becomes per-agent gap detection, not replay control.

Startup check: if the configured pool id disagrees with the pool the signing key implies, refuse to start with a message naming both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent id config field defaults to slugified hostname and is logged at startup
- [ ] Sealed batches carry the agent id in the header; every line carries `metsuke` provenance
- [ ] Sequence number advances per agent
- [ ] Startup refusal names both the configured pool id and the key-implied one (config suite)
- [ ] Metrics and trace lines have the same line shape (one duckdb query reads both)

## Blocked by

Wire container ticket, trace-parsing ticket.
close_reason: Agent id, per-line metsuke provenance, pool-id startup refusal

title: Server ingest strip, new object keys, two-agent e2e
description:
## What to build

The complete accepted path becomes: allowlist lookup → derive pool from the verifying key → per-pool and global rate limits → Ed25519 verify over the body → PUT with metadata headers. The server never decompresses and never parses a payload. Removed as a consequence: decompression limits, payload parsing, schema-version gating, pool-id cross-checking (the pool-id request header is dropped — it carried nothing the key does not prove), timestamp-skew refusal, replay-counter refusal. max_body_bytes on the compressed bytes is the only size limit. Tests for removed checks are deleted with them; the intake suite shrinks to allowlist, key-belongs-to-pool, signature.

Objects are keyed `v1/<date>/<uuid7>-<pool>-<agent>-<metrics|logs>.jsonl.zst`. Time-major; UUIDv7 stamped at upload so a late spool flush still sorts after everything synced — one start-after cursor is the whole delta-sync protocol. Uniqueness comes from the UUIDv7 alone, never the clock, sequence number, or agent id. Pool segment derives from the verifying key, not the header. Date segment is the server's receipt date.

Per-pool rate limit default: 100 submissions/hour (~16× headroom over 6 agents at one upload/hour) — a runaway-agent backstop, not abuse control. All limits are configuration.

The replay-counter refusal is keyed per pool, so today a second agent for the same pool is rejected as a replay — the motivating bug. metsuke-jfb.3 already made the agent's own counter per-agent gap detection (`envelope::Envelope::counter`); this ticket is the server half, and ADR 0002 (replay counter) is deleted in the commit that removes the code it describes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Intake suite covers exactly: allowlist, key-belongs-to-pool, signature
- [ ] Object keys match the scheme; pool segment derives from the verifying key
- [ ] HTTP suite asserts status codes for each refusal that remains
- [ ] e2e VM test runs two agents for one pool with different agent ids and asserts both objects land (regression test for the motivating multi-machine bug)
- [ ] ADR 0002 deleted in the same change

## Blocked by

Agent identity ticket.

title: Stateless cold-key-only server: Calidus, db-sync, SQLite all deleted
description:
## What to build

Authority becomes cold-key-only: pool identity is derived from the cold verifying key, the only claim under the signature. Calidus resolution is removed entirely — the directory, the CIP-151 witness check, the db-sync client, and the postgres dependency. Participants polled in favour of cold-key signing.

Server state becomes none: the SQLite index, counter reservations, and rebuild path are deleted along with rusqlite. The listing route calls ListObjectsV2 with the client's prefix and start-after; list_max_rows clamps to 1000 (S3's cap) so one request is one upstream page and truncated comes straight from IsTruncated. The object route GETs and passes through; the existence pre-check is deleted and the upstream 404 passes through. The rate limiter stays in memory — losing it on restart is harmless. The bucket is the source of truth, as it already was.

Docs land in the deleting commits: ADRs 0003, 0008, 0009 deleted; ADR 0005 trimmed to the part still true (archive stores raw signed bytes, source of truth; the SQLite-index sentence goes). CONTEXT.md loses Calidus Key, Registration, Nonce, Witness, Revocation; gains Agent (one machine's reporter, several per pool), Sequence Number, Frame. No new ADRs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server links no postgres, no rusqlite, no csv
- [ ] Calidus, db-sync, index and rebuild suites deleted with the code they cover
- [ ] Listing route is a ListObjectsV2 passthrough; truncated mirrors IsTruncated
- [ ] Object route passes upstream 404 through
- [ ] Server restart loses nothing but in-memory rate-limit windows
- [ ] ADRs 0003/0008/0009 deleted, 0005 trimmed, CONTEXT.md updated, in the deleting commits

## Blocked by

Server ingest strip ticket.

title: HTTP layer: hyper replaces tiny_http
description:
## What to build

hyper + hyper-util replace tiny_http. Why nothing else will do: tiny_http 0.12 exposes no socket timeout and no way to skip its drain-on-drop, so neither of metsuke-a3a's failure modes (60-byte request declaring 4 GB Content-Length drives 4.2 GB VmSize and a MemoryMax kill; a trickling body stalls all ingest) is fixable in our own code. Sequenced after the routes have shrunk, which makes it a smaller change.

- Read, write and idle timeouts, all configuration (NixOS module options)
- Body cap via a limited-body wrapper, no drain-on-drop allocation
- Global concurrent-request cap, default 64, enforced at accept
- The object download route streams the upstream body through rather than buffering

Routing stays a match on four paths — no router crate. TLS and IP-keyed limits remain the reverse proxy's; the proxy is defence in depth, no longer what any correctness argument rests on.

Closes metsuke-a3a; also resolves metsuke-4zo.72 (download buffers whole object) and .73 (download stalls ingest).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A request declaring a large Content-Length without sending a body neither allocates nor stalls other requests — as a test, not an inspection (metsuke-a3a's acceptance criterion)
- [ ] HTTP suite: status codes for remaining refusals, 401 challenge on developer routes, body-size cap
- [ ] Downloads stream; a slow developer download does not stall ingest
- [ ] Timeouts, body cap, concurrency cap all NixOS module options
- [ ] metsuke-a3a closed by this ticket's landing commit

## Blocked by

Stateless cold-key-only server ticket.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Keep the transport out of the routing signature.

tiny_http's version does this wrong: `route` takes `&mut tiny_http::Request` and returns a private `Answer`, so the only way to reach it is over a socket. tests/binary.rs spawns the binary for 36 tests and SIGKILLs it in Drop, so LLVM flushes no profile: http.rs, intake.rs, ratelimit.rs and developer.rs all measure 0% under `cargo llvm-cov --test binary` while every one of those tests passes. The workspace 79.37% is a floor, not a measurement.

For hyper: routing takes decoded parts (method, path, headers, body reader + declared length) and returns a public status/body value. No hyper type in the signature. Then the HTTP suite acceptance criterion above is unit tests over values, and the socket tests are only the ones that must be — timeouts, the drain/allocation behaviour, streaming.

title: Allowlist generator: offline CSV to application-code-checked TOML
description:
## What to build

The application-code gate moves off the serving path into its own binary or nushell script. It reads the registration CSV, checks each pool's application code against the code in that pool's current on-chain registration metadata, and emits the allowlist TOML block. Run once when the server configuration is generated — the gate runs once and never touches the serving path, so the server links no postgres, tokio-via-postgres, or csv.

CSV normalisation needed: three optional pool-id columns flatten to one list per applicant, and at least one row has a leading space before a pool id.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Emits a TOML allowlist block the server config accepts
- [ ] Each pool's application code is checked against its current on-chain registration metadata
- [ ] The three pool-id columns flatten to one list per applicant; whitespace is trimmed
- [ ] Not part of the serving binary

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

title: Fetch tool crate
description:
## What to build

A new, separate crate — not a subcommand of the server or agent. List a prefix → download objects after the cursor → advance the cursor in a local state file. Objects are written to disk verbatim, so the downloaded bytes remain signature-checkable and directly readable by duckdb. Resumes after an interruption without restarting the download. Authenticates as the shared developer account against the server's routes (direct bucket credentials are not currently available).

One start-after cursor is the whole delta-sync protocol; pool, agent and kind are readable off the key, so filtering a listing (just metrics, just logs, just one pool) needs no downloads. The header's schema version tells the tool what it pulled; it gates nothing on the server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sync is one command: list after cursor, download, advance cursor in a local state file
- [ ] Downloaded bytes are byte-identical to the archived object (signature re-verifiable)
- [ ] duckdb reads downloaded objects directly, no unpacking
- [ ] Interrupting and re-running resumes rather than restarting
- [ ] Listing filters by pool/agent/kind prefix without downloading

## Blocked by

Server ingest strip ticket, stateless server ticket.

title: A row's wire cost is computed in two crates with nothing tying the halves
description:
What one spooled row costs in a sealed payload is now split: `push_capped`
(crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs) stores text + newline in the `bytes` column, and
`RowBudget::per_row_bytes` carries the provenance stamp from
`envelope::provenance_bytes`. Nothing ties the halves together.

A framing change in `envelope::payload_lines` that misses either half makes the
agent's `upload_batch_max_bytes` disagree with the server's
`max_decompressed_bytes` silently — the wedge metsuke-4zo.96 already fixed once,
reachable again.

Fix: one function in metsuke-wire owning a row's whole wire cost, which the
spool column and the budget both read.

title: Migrate pre-existing test-key copies to tests/support
description: crates/metsuke/tests/{delivery,wire,keys,sntp?}.rs each construct SigningKey::from_bytes(&[7u8; 32]) inline; tests/support/mod.rs (added in metsuke-4zo.5 review round 1) owns test_key(). Move the pre-existing copies over. Mechanical.

title: Cold-key check has two sites: intake and verify
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs submit() and src/verify.rs verify() both run the ADR-0003 key check followed by envelope::open. The primitives are shared (PoolId::from_cold_key, envelope::open); the ordering is not.

Matters for metsuke-4zo.8: the Calidus path has to join at both sites or a Calidus-signed object stays unverifiable in the archive while verifying fine on ingest.

Fix while doing .8: one authenticate(pool_id, vkey, signature, bytes, max) -> Result<Envelope, AuthError>, mapped to intake::Rejection on the ingest path and to VerifyError on the archive path.
close_reason: authenticate() in authority.rs is now the one check-then-open sequence for intake and verify

title: Config errors under [archive] point at the table, not the field
description:
config.rs ArchiveConfig is #[serde(tag = "kind")]; serde's internally-tagged path buffers the table into a Content value and drops toml's spans. So request_timeout_secs = 0 reports 'TOML parse error at line 16 | [archive] | invalid value: integer 0, expected a nonzero u64' — no field name. [ingest] fields point at their own line and column.

Pinned by tests/config.rs a_refused_value_is_pointed_at_by_its_own_line, which asserts both halves.

Fix: represent the archive kind without an internally-tagged enum, or validate the block a second time with a spanned deserializer.
